source.text: וַיְהִ֞י בְּבֹ֨א דָוִ֧ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֛יו צִֽקְלַ֖ג בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י וַעֲמָלֵקִ֣י פָֽשְׁט֗וּ אֶל־נֶ֨גֶב֙ וְאֶל־צִ֣קְלַ֔ג וַיַּכּוּ֙ אֶת־צִ֣קְלַ֔ג וַיִּשְׂרְפ֥וּ אֹתָ֖הּ בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was when came David and his men [to] Ziklag on the day the third, and [the] Amalekites had raided against [the] Negev and against Ziklag, and they had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.

en.L: And it happened, when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, [that the] Amalekites had made a raid on the Negev and on Ziklag, and they had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.
en.B: On the third day David and his men reached Ziklag. The Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag. They had attacked Ziklag and burned it down.
en.R: On the third day after they left the Philistine army, David and his men got back to Ziklag. While they were away, the Amalekites had made a raid on the Negev, the dry land in the south. They had attacked Ziklag and burned it down.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando David y sus hombres llegaron a Siclag al tercer día, los amalecitas habían hecho una incursión contra el Néguev y contra Siclag, y habían herido a Siclag y le habían prendido fuego.
es.B: Al tercer día David y sus hombres llegaron a Siclag. Los amalecitas habían hecho una incursión en el Néguev y en Siclag. Habían atacado Siclag y la habían incendiado.
es.R: Al tercer día después de dejar el ejército filisteo, David y sus hombres volvieron a Siclag. Mientras estaban fuera, los amalecitas habían atacado el Néguev, la tierra seca del sur. Habían atacado Siclag y la habían quemado.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand David et ses hommes arrivèrent à Tsiqlag le troisième jour, [que les] Amalécites avaient fait une incursion dans le Néguev et à Tsiqlag, et ils avaient frappé Tsiqlag et l’avaient incendiée.
fr.B: Le troisième jour, David et ses hommes arrivèrent à Tsiqlag. Les Amalécites avaient fait une incursion dans le Néguev et à Tsiqlag. Ils avaient attaqué Tsiqlag et l’avaient livrée aux flammes.
fr.R: Le troisième jour après avoir quitté l’armée des Philistins, David et ses hommes sont arrivés à Tsiqlag. Pendant leur absence, les Amalécites avaient attaqué le Néguev, la région sèche du sud. Ils avaient attaqué Tsiqlag et l’avaient brûlée.

sw.L: Ikawa Daudi na watu wake walipofika Siklagi siku ya tatu, Waamaleki walikuwa wamevamia Negebu na Siklagi, nao walikuwa wameupiga Siklagi na kuuteketeza kwa moto.
sw.B: Siku ya tatu Daudi na watu wake wakafika Siklagi. Waamaleki walikuwa wamevamia Negebu na Siklagi. Walikuwa wameushambulia Siklagi na kuuteketeza kwa moto.
sw.R: Siku ya tatu baada ya kuliacha jeshi la Wafilisti, Daudi na watu wake wakarudi Siklagi. Walipokuwa mbali, Waamaleki walikuwa wamevamia Negebu, nchi kavu ya kusini. Walikuwa wameushambulia Siklagi na kuuteketeza kwa moto.

vi.L: Khi Đa-vít và những người của ông đến Xiếc-lác vào ngày thứ ba, thì người A-ma-léc đã đột kích miền Nê-ghép và Xiếc-lác; họ đã đánh Xiếc-lác và lấy lửa đốt thành.
vi.B: Ngày thứ ba, Đa-vít và thuộc hạ về đến Xiếc-lác. Người A-ma-léc đã đột kích miền Nê-ghép và Xiếc-lác. Họ đã tấn công Xiếc-lác và đốt rụi thành.
vi.R: Đến ngày thứ ba sau khi rời quân Phi-li-tin, Đa-vít và thuộc hạ về đến Xiếc-lác. Trong khi họ vắng mặt, người A-ma-léc đã đột kích miền Nê-ghép, là vùng đất khô cằn ở phía nam. Họ đã tấn công Xiếc-lác và đốt rụi thành.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗과 그의 부하들이 사흘째 되는 날 시글락에 이르렀을 때, 아말렉 사람들이 네겝과 시글락을 습격하여 시글락을 치고 불로 태워 버렸다.
ko.B: 사흘째 되는 날 다윗과 그의 부하들은 시글락에 이르렀다. 그사이에 아말렉 사람들이 네겝과 시글락을 습격했었다. 그들은 시글락을 쳐서 불태워 버렸다.
ko.R: 다윗과 그의 부하들은 블레셋 군대를 떠난 지 사흘째 되는 날 시글락에 돌아왔다. 그들이 없는 동안 아말렉 사람들이 남쪽의 메마른 땅 네겝을 습격했었다. 그들은 시글락을 쳐서 불태워 버렸다.

decisions.choice: Ziklag on the third day: David's town, reached on the third day after he left the Philistine army
decisions.reason: Achish king of Gath had given Ziklag to David (27:6). The Philistine commanders had sent David away from their army at Aphek, and he left early in the morning to go back to the land of the Philistines (29:10-11). "The third day" counts from that departure; the march south to Ziklag was a long one.

decisions.choice: the Amalekites had raided the Negev: a sudden raid on the dry south country
decisions.reason: The verb means to dash out and strip a place, the word used of David's own raids on the Amalekites and their neighbors (27:8). The Negev is the dry southern land of Judah and the Philistine border. While David and the Philistine army were away in the north, the south lay open.

decisions.choice: had raided ... had struck ... had burned: things that happened before David arrived
decisions.reason: The verse opens with David's arrival and then tells, in the past, what the Amalekites had already done while he was gone. Verse 3 shows what David found.

decisions.choice: after they left the Philistine army; the dry land in the south
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the third day" counts from (m1) and explains the place name Negev once.

decisions.choice: plus-que-parfait ("avaient fait", "avaient frappé", "avaient incendiée")
decisions.reason: What the Amalekites had done before David arrived (m3) takes the French pluperfect at every level, through verse 3.

decisions.choice: "그사이에" / "그들이 없는 동안" (meanwhile) to mark events before David's arrival
decisions.reason: The raid had already happened when David arrived (meaning decision m3); Korean has no pluperfect, so a time word places it, with "-었었다".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁבּ֨וּ אֶת־הַנָּשִׁ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּהּ֙ מִקָּטֹ֣ן וְעַד־גָּד֔וֹל לֹ֥א הֵמִ֖יתוּ אִ֑ישׁ וַיִּֽנְהֲג֔וּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ לְדַרְכָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they had taken captive the women who [were] in it, from small and unto great; not they had killed anyone, and they had driven [them] off and gone on their way.

en.L: And they had taken captive the women who [were] in it, from small to great. They had not killed anyone, but they had driven [them] off and gone on their way.
en.B: They had taken captive the women who were there, young and old alike. They had killed no one, but had carried them all off and gone on their way.
en.R: They had captured the women and everyone else in the town, young and old. They did not kill anyone. They took them all away with them.

es.L: Y habían llevado cautivas a las mujeres que [estaban] en ella, desde el pequeño hasta el grande. No habían matado a nadie, sino que [se los] habían llevado y habían seguido su camino.
es.B: Se habían llevado cautivas a las mujeres que había allí, jóvenes y viejas por igual. No habían matado a nadie, sino que se los habían llevado a todos y habían seguido su camino.
es.R: Habían capturado a las mujeres y a todos los demás que había en el pueblo, jóvenes y viejos. No mataron a nadie. Se los llevaron a todos.

fr.L: Et ils avaient emmené captives les femmes qui [y étaient], du petit au grand ; ils n’avaient tué personne, mais ils les avaient emmenés et avaient continué leur chemin.
fr.B: Ils avaient emmené captives les femmes qui s’y trouvaient, petits et grands. Ils n’avaient tué personne, mais ils avaient emmené tout le monde et étaient repartis.
fr.R: Ils avaient fait prisonniers les femmes et tous les autres habitants de la ville, jeunes et vieux. Ils n’avaient tué personne. Ils les avaient tous emmenés avec eux.

sw.L: Walikuwa wamewateka wanawake waliokuwa ndani yake, wadogo kwa wakubwa. Hawakumwua mtu yeyote, ila waliwachukua, wakaenda zao.
sw.B: Walikuwa wamewateka wanawake waliokuwa humo, vijana kwa wazee. Hawakumwua mtu yeyote, ila waliwachukua wote, wakaenda zao.
sw.R: Walikuwa wamewateka wanawake na watu wengine wote mjini, vijana kwa wazee. Hawakumwua mtu yeyote. Waliwachukua wote pamoja nao.

vi.L: Họ đã bắt làm phu tù các phụ nữ trong thành, từ nhỏ đến lớn. Họ không giết ai, nhưng đã lùa [họ] đi và tiếp tục lên đường.
vi.B: Họ đã bắt các phụ nữ trong thành làm phu tù, cả trẻ lẫn già. Họ không giết ai, nhưng bắt hết đem đi rồi tiếp tục lên đường.
vi.R: Họ đã bắt các phụ nữ và mọi người khác trong thành, cả trẻ lẫn già. Họ không giết ai cả. Họ dẫn tất cả đi theo mình.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 그 안에 있던 여자들을 작은 사람부터 큰 사람까지 사로잡았다. 그들은 아무도 죽이지 않고 [그들을] 몰고 자기들의 길을 갔다.
ko.B: 그들은 그곳에 있던 여자들을 젊은이와 늙은이 할 것 없이 모두 사로잡아 갔다. 아무도 죽이지 않고 모두 끌고 자기들의 길을 갔다.
ko.R: 그들은 여자들과 마을에 있던 모든 사람을 사로잡았다. 젊은이와 늙은이를 가리지 않았다. 그들은 아무도 죽이지 않고 모두 끌고 갔다.

decisions.choice: from small to great: all of them, young and old
decisions.reason: The pair "small ... great" means everyone, whatever their age or rank (5:9; 30:19). Verse 3 shows that the captives were the men's wives, sons and daughters: the fighting men were all away with David.

decisions.choice: they killed no one, but drove them off: the captives were taken alive
decisions.reason: The Amalekites took people as plunder, to keep or sell as slaves. David had done the opposite on his raids, leaving no one alive (27:9, 11). The fact that the captives were alive makes the rescue possible.

decisions.choice: drove off: led away like a herd
decisions.reason: The verb is used for driving animals (verse 20) and for leading captives away (Genesis 31:26).

decisions.choice: the women and everyone else in the town
decisions.reason: Readable names the children as well, as verse 3 does, so that the reader is not left thinking only the women were taken.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א דָוִ֤ד וַֽאֲנָשָׁיו֙ אֶל־הָעִ֔יר וְהִנֵּ֥ה שְׂרוּפָ֖ה בָּאֵ֑שׁ וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֛ם וּבְנֵיהֶ֥ם וּבְנֹתֵיהֶ֖ם נִשְׁבּֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came David and his men to the city, and there! [it was] burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.

en.L: And David and his men came to the town, and look, [it was] burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.
en.B: When David and his men came to the town, they found it burned down, and their wives, sons and daughters taken captive.
en.R: When David and his men got to the town, they saw that it had been burned. Their wives, sons and daughters had been taken away as prisoners.

es.L: Y llegaron David y sus hombres a la ciudad, y he aquí [que estaba] quemada con fuego, y sus mujeres y sus hijos y sus hijas habían sido llevados cautivos.
es.B: Cuando David y sus hombres llegaron a la ciudad, la encontraron incendiada, y a sus esposas, hijos e hijas, llevados cautivos.
es.R: Cuando David y sus hombres llegaron al pueblo, vieron que lo habían quemado. Se habían llevado presos a sus esposas, a sus hijos y a sus hijas.

fr.L: Et David et ses hommes arrivèrent à la ville, et voici, [elle était] incendiée, et leurs femmes, et leurs fils, et leurs filles avaient été emmenés captifs.
fr.B: Quand David et ses hommes arrivèrent à la ville, ils la trouvèrent incendiée, et leurs femmes, leurs fils et leurs filles emmenés captifs.
fr.R: Quand David et ses hommes sont arrivés à la ville, ils ont vu qu’elle avait été brûlée. Leurs femmes, leurs fils et leurs filles avaient été emmenés comme prisonniers.

sw.L: Daudi na watu wake wakafika mjini, na tazama, [ulikuwa] umeteketezwa kwa moto, na wake zao na wana wao na binti zao walikuwa wametekwa.
sw.B: Daudi na watu wake walipofika mjini, wakaukuta umeteketezwa kwa moto, na wake zao, wana wao na binti zao wametekwa.
sw.R: Daudi na watu wake walipofika mjini, wakaona kwamba umechomwa moto. Wake zao, wana wao na binti zao walikuwa wamechukuliwa mateka.

vi.L: Đa-vít và những người của ông đến thành, kìa, [thành đã] bị lửa đốt, còn vợ, con trai và con gái của họ đã bị bắt làm phu tù.
vi.B: Khi Đa-vít và thuộc hạ đến thành, họ thấy thành đã bị đốt cháy, còn vợ, con trai và con gái của họ đã bị bắt đi làm phu tù.
vi.R: Khi Đa-vít và thuộc hạ về đến thành, họ thấy thành đã bị đốt cháy. Vợ, con trai và con gái của họ đã bị bắt đi làm tù binh.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗과 그의 부하들이 그 성읍에 와 보니, 보라, [성읍은] 불에 타 버렸고, 그들의 아내들과 아들들과 딸들은 사로잡혀 갔다.
ko.B: 다윗과 그의 부하들이 성읍에 와 보니, 성읍은 불타 버렸고 그들의 아내와 아들딸들은 사로잡혀 가고 없었다.
ko.R: 다윗과 그의 부하들이 마을에 와 보니, 마을은 불타 있었다. 그들의 아내와 아들딸들은 포로로 끌려가고 없었다.

decisions.choice: and look, burned: the scene as the men saw it on arrival
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "behold" moves the telling to what the arriving men saw with their own eyes: smoke and ruins and empty houses.

decisions.choice: the city: Ziklag, a small town
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for "city" covers any settlement with houses, walled or not. Here it is Ziklag (verse 1).

decisions.choice: they found / they saw
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "look" into a verb of seeing, which is what it marks (m1).

source.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א דָוִ֜ד וְהָעָ֧ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֛וֹ אֶת־קוֹלָ֖ם וַיִּבְכּ֑וּ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֵין־בָּהֶ֛ם כֹּ֖חַ לִבְכּֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And lifted up David and the people who [were] with him their voice and they wept, until that there was not in them strength to weep.

en.L: And David and the people who [were] with him lifted up their voice and wept, until there was no strength in them to weep.
en.B: David and the troops with him wept aloud until they had no strength left to weep.
en.R: David and his soldiers cried out loud until they were too weak to cry anymore.

es.L: Y alzaron David y el pueblo que [estaba] con él su voz y lloraron, hasta que no les quedaron fuerzas para llorar.
es.B: David y las tropas que estaban con él lloraron a gritos hasta que no les quedaron fuerzas para llorar.
es.R: David y sus soldados lloraron a gritos hasta que estuvieron demasiado débiles para seguir llorando.

fr.L: Et David et le peuple qui [était] avec lui élevèrent la voix et pleurèrent, jusqu’à ce qu’il n’y ait plus en eux de force pour pleurer.
fr.B: David et la troupe qui était avec lui pleurèrent à grands cris, jusqu’à ne plus avoir la force de pleurer.
fr.R: David et ses soldats ont pleuré très fort, jusqu’à ce qu’ils n’aient plus la force de pleurer.

sw.L: Daudi na watu waliokuwa pamoja naye wakainua sauti yao, wakalia, mpaka hawakuwa na nguvu tena ya kulia.
sw.B: Daudi na askari waliokuwa pamoja naye wakalia kwa sauti mpaka wakaishiwa nguvu ya kulia.
sw.R: Daudi na askari wake wakalia kwa sauti kubwa mpaka wakachoka hata wasiweze kulia tena.

vi.L: Đa-vít và dân chúng ở với ông cất tiếng khóc cho đến khi họ không còn sức để khóc nữa.
vi.B: Đa-vít và quân lính theo ông khóc lớn cho đến khi không còn sức để khóc nữa.
vi.R: Đa-vít và quân lính của ông khóc to cho đến khi kiệt sức, không khóc được nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗과 그와 함께 있던 백성이 소리를 높여 울었는데, 울 힘이 없을 때까지 울었다.
ko.B: 다윗과 그와 함께 있던 군인들은 더 이상 울 힘이 없을 때까지 소리 내어 울었다.
ko.R: 다윗과 그의 군인들은 너무 울어서 더 울 힘도 없을 때까지 큰 소리로 울었다.

decisions.choice: lifted up their voice and wept: wept aloud
decisions.reason: The phrase describes open, loud mourning (11:4; Genesis 27:38; Judges 2:4).

decisions.choice: the people: David's fighting men
decisions.reason: The people "with him" are the 600 men who followed David (verse 9; 27:2).

decisions.choice: troops (Balanced), soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The people" here are an army in the field, so Balanced says "troops" and Readable "soldiers", as elsewhere in 1 Samuel.

source.text: וּשְׁתֵּ֥י נְשֵֽׁי־דָוִ֖ד נִשְׁבּ֑וּ אֲחִינֹ֨עַם֙ הַיִּזְרְעֵלִ֔ית וַאֲבִיגַ֕יִל אֵ֖שֶׁת נָבָ֥ל הַֽכַּרְמְלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] two wives of David had been taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail [the] wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

en.L: And the two wives of David had been taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
en.B: David's two wives had been taken captive too: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal of Carmel.
en.R: David's two wives had also been taken: Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, and Abigail, whose first husband Nabal had come from Carmel.

es.L: Y las dos mujeres de David habían sido llevadas cautivas, Ahinoam la jezreelita y Abigail, la mujer de Nabal el de Carmel.
es.B: También se habían llevado cautivas a las dos esposas de David: Ahinoam de Jezreel y Abigail, la viuda de Nabal de Carmel.
es.R: También se habían llevado a las dos esposas de David: Ahinoam, del pueblo de Jezreel, y Abigail, cuyo primer esposo, Nabal, había sido de Carmel.

fr.L: Et les deux femmes de David avaient été emmenées captives, Ahinoam la Jizreélite et Abigaïl, la femme de Nabal le Carmélite.
fr.B: Les deux femmes de David avaient été emmenées elles aussi : Ahinoam de Jizreël et Abigaïl, la veuve de Nabal de Carmel.
fr.R: Les deux femmes de David avaient aussi été emmenées : Ahinoam, de la ville de Jizreël, et Abigaïl, dont le premier mari, Nabal, venait de Carmel.

sw.L: Wake wawili wa Daudi walikuwa wametekwa, Ahinoamu Myezreeli na Abigaili mke wa Nabali Mkarmeli.
sw.B: Wake wawili wa Daudi nao walikuwa wametekwa: Ahinoamu wa Yezreeli na Abigaili, mjane wa Nabali wa Karmeli.
sw.R: Wake wawili wa Daudi nao walikuwa wamechukuliwa: Ahinoamu wa mji wa Yezreeli, na Abigaili, ambaye mume wake wa kwanza Nabali alitoka Karmeli.

vi.L: Hai vợ của Đa-vít cũng đã bị bắt làm phu tù: A-hi-nô-am người Gít-rê-ên và A-bi-ga-in, vợ của Na-banh người Cạt-mên.
vi.B: Hai vợ của Đa-vít cũng bị bắt đi: A-hi-nô-am người Gít-rê-ên và A-bi-ga-in, vợ góa của Na-banh người Cạt-mên.
vi.R: Hai vợ của Đa-vít cũng bị bắt đi: A-hi-nô-am ở thành Gít-rê-ên, và A-bi-ga-in, người có chồng trước là Na-banh ở Cạt-mên.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗의 두 아내, 이스르엘 여자 아히노암과 갈멜 사람 나발의 아내였던 아비가일도 사로잡혀 갔다.
ko.B: 다윗의 두 아내, 곧 이스르엘 여자 아히노암과 갈멜 사람 나발의 아내였던 아비가일도 사로잡혀 갔다.
ko.R: 다윗의 두 아내도 끌려갔다. 이스르엘 마을 출신 아히노암과, 갈멜 사람 나발의 아내였던 아비가일이었다.

decisions.choice: Ahinoam the Jezreelite, Abigail of Nabal the Carmelite: David's two wives, both from Judah
decisions.reason: David married both women while he was a fugitive (25:42-43; 27:3). Jezreel here is a town in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15:56), not the better-known Jezreel in the north. Carmel is a town south of Hebron (25:2), not Mount Carmel.

decisions.choice: the wife of Nabal: Nabal's widow
decisions.reason: Nabal had died (25:38-39), and David then married Abigail. She is still named by her first husband, as she is in 27:3.

decisions.choice: the widow of Nabal; whose first husband Nabal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that Nabal was dead (m2), so the reader does not think Abigail had two living husbands.

source.text: וַתֵּ֨צֶר לְדָוִ֜ד מְאֹ֗ד כִּֽי־אָמְר֤וּ הָעָם֙ לְסָקְל֔וֹ כִּֽי־מָ֨רָה֙ נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ עַל־בָּנָ֣יו וְעַל־בְּנֹתָ֑יו וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֣ק דָּוִ֔ד בַּיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was distressing to David greatly, for said the people to stone him, for was bitter [the] soul of all the people, each over his sons and over his daughters; and strengthened himself David in Yahweh his God.

en.L: And David was in great distress, for the people spoke of stoning him, for the soul of all the people was bitter, each man over his sons and over his daughters. But David strengthened himself in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.
en.B: David was in deep distress, because the troops were talking about stoning him. Each of them was bitter over his sons and daughters. Yet David drew strength from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.
en.R: David was in great trouble, because his soldiers were talking about killing him by throwing stones at him. They were all full of grief and anger over their lost sons and daughters. But David found new courage in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.

es.L: Y David estaba muy angustiado, porque el pueblo hablaba de apedrearlo, pues el alma de todo el pueblo estaba amargada, cada uno por sus hijos y por sus hijas. Pero David se fortaleció en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} su Dios.
es.B: David estaba muy angustiado, porque las tropas hablaban de apedrearlo. Todos estaban amargados por sus hijos y sus hijas. Pero David encontró fuerzas en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} su Dios.
es.R: David estaba en un gran aprieto, porque sus soldados hablaban de matarlo a pedradas. Todos estaban llenos de dolor y de rabia por sus hijos y sus hijas perdidos. Pero David recobró el ánimo en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} su Dios.

fr.L: Et David fut dans une grande détresse, car le peuple parlait de le lapider, car l’âme de tout le peuple était amère, chacun au sujet de ses fils et de ses filles. Mais David se fortifia dans {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} son Dieu.
fr.B: David se trouva dans une profonde détresse, car la troupe parlait de le lapider. Tous étaient pleins d’amertume à cause de leurs fils et de leurs filles. Mais David puisa des forces dans {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} son Dieu.
fr.R: David était dans une situation très difficile, parce que ses soldats parlaient de le tuer en lui jetant des pierres. Ils étaient tous pleins de chagrin et de colère à cause de leurs fils et de leurs filles disparus. Mais David a retrouvé courage auprès {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} son Dieu.

sw.L: Daudi akawa katika dhiki kubwa, kwa maana watu walisema juu ya kumpiga kwa mawe, kwa sababu nafsi ya watu wote ilikuwa na uchungu, kila mtu kwa ajili ya wanawe na binti zake. Lakini Daudi akajitia nguvu katika {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wake.
sw.B: Daudi akawa katika dhiki kuu, kwa sababu askari walikuwa wakizungumza juu ya kumpiga kwa mawe. Kila mmoja alikuwa na uchungu kwa ajili ya wanawe na binti zake. Lakini Daudi akapata nguvu kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wake.
sw.R: Daudi akawa katika taabu kubwa, kwa sababu askari wake walikuwa wakizungumza juu ya kumwua kwa kumpiga mawe. Wote walijawa na huzuni na hasira kwa ajili ya wana na binti zao waliopotea. Lakini Daudi akapata ujasiri mpya katika {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wake.

vi.L: Đa-vít rất khốn quẫn, vì dân chúng nói đến việc ném đá ông, vì linh hồn toàn dân đều cay đắng, mỗi người vì con trai và con gái mình. Nhưng Đa-vít làm cho mình mạnh mẽ trong {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của mình.
vi.B: Đa-vít vô cùng khốn đốn, vì quân lính bàn đến việc ném đá ông. Ai nấy đều cay đắng vì con trai con gái mình. Nhưng Đa-vít được thêm sức mạnh nơi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của mình.
vi.R: Đa-vít gặp nguy khốn lớn, vì quân lính của ông bàn nhau ném đá cho ông chết. Ai nấy đều đau đớn và giận dữ vì con trai con gái mình bị bắt mất. Nhưng Đa-vít tìm được can đảm mới nơi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của mình.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗은 몹시 괴로웠다. 백성이 그를 돌로 치자고 말했기 때문이다. 모든 백성이 저마다 자기 아들들과 딸들 때문에 영혼이 쓰라렸던 것이다. 그러나 다윗은 그의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 안에서 스스로 힘을 얻었다.
ko.B: 다윗은 큰 곤경에 빠졌다. 군인들이 그를 돌로 쳐 죽이자고 말했기 때문이다. 그들은 저마다 자기 아들딸들 때문에 마음이 몹시 쓰라렸다. 그러나 다윗은 자기 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 힘을 얻었다.
ko.R: 다윗은 큰 어려움에 빠졌다. 그의 군인들이 그를 돌로 쳐 죽이자고 말하고 있었기 때문이다. 그들은 모두 잃어버린 아들딸들 때문에 슬프고 화가 나 있었다. 그러나 다윗은 자기 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 의지하여 새 힘을 얻었다.

decisions.choice: David was in great distress: hemmed in, by grief and by danger
decisions.reason: The verb means to be narrow or tight, to be pressed on every side. David has lost his own family, and now his own men turn on him.

decisions.choice: the soul of all the people was bitter: grief mixed with anger
decisions.reason: Bitterness of soul is deep grief that can turn to anger (1:10 of Hannah; 22:2; Judges 18:25). The men blame David for leaving the town unguarded.

decisions.choice: spoke of stoning him: a mob ready to kill its leader
decisions.reason: Stoning was the way a crowd put someone to death (Exodus 17:4, where the people are about to stone Moses; Numbers 14:10).

decisions.choice: David strengthened himself in the LORD his God: he took courage from the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself strong or firm. David's strength comes from the LORD whom he calls his God, and he turns at once to ask the LORD what to do (verses 7-8). Saul, at the same time, finds no answer from the LORD (28:6).

decisions.choice: drew strength (Balanced), found new courage (Readable)
decisions.reason: The reflexive "strengthened himself" is put as finding strength or courage, which is what it means in this setting.

decisions.choice: full of grief and anger
decisions.reason: Readable explains "bitter of soul" (m2) instead of keeping the picture.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶל־אֶבְיָתָ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ בֶּן־אֲחִימֶ֔לֶךְ הַגִּֽישָׁה־נָּ֥א לִ֖י הָאֵפֹ֑ד וַיַּגֵּ֧שׁ אֶבְיָתָ֛ר אֶת־הָאֵפֹ֖ד אֶל־דָּוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, Bring near please to me the ephod. And brought near Abiathar the ephod to David.

en.L: And David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, "Bring the ephod near to me, please." And Abiathar brought the ephod near to David.
en.B: David told Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, "Bring the ephod here to me, please." So Abiathar brought the ephod to David.
en.R: David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, "Please bring me the ephod." The ephod was the priest's vest used to ask God for answers. Abiathar brought it to David.

es.L: Y dijo David al sacerdote Abiatar, hijo de Ahimelec: «Acércame, te ruego, el efod». Y Abiatar acercó el efod a David.
es.B: David le dijo al sacerdote Abiatar, el hijo de Ahimelec: «Por favor, tráeme el efod». Y Abiatar le llevó el efod a David.
es.R: David le dijo al sacerdote Abiatar, el hijo de Ahimelec: «Por favor, tráeme el efod». El efod era el chaleco del sacerdote que se usaba para pedirle respuestas a Dios. Abiatar se lo llevó a David.

fr.L: Et David dit à Abiathar le prêtre, fils d’Ahimélek : « Approche donc l’éphod vers moi. » Et Abiathar approcha l’éphod vers David.
fr.B: David dit au prêtre Abiathar, fils d’Ahimélek : « Apporte-moi l’éphod, je te prie. » Et Abiathar apporta l’éphod à David.
fr.R: David a dit à Abiathar le prêtre, le fils d’Ahimélek : « S’il te plaît, apporte-moi l’éphod. » L’éphod était le vêtement du prêtre qui servait à demander des réponses à Dieu. Abiathar l’a apporté à David.

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia Abiathari kuhani, mwana wa Ahimeleki, "Tafadhali niletee efodi karibu." Abiathari akamletea Daudi efodi karibu.
sw.B: Daudi akamwambia Abiathari kuhani, mwana wa Ahimeleki, "Tafadhali niletee efodi hapa." Basi Abiathari akamletea Daudi efodi.
sw.R: Daudi akamwambia Abiathari kuhani, mwana wa Ahimeleki, "Tafadhali niletee efodi." Efodi ilikuwa vazi la kuhani lililotumiwa kumwuliza Mungu majibu. Abiathari akamletea Daudi.

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với thầy tế lễ A-bi-a-tha, con trai A-hi-mê-léc: "Xin đem áo ê-phót lại gần tôi." A-bi-a-tha đem áo ê-phót lại gần Đa-vít.
vi.B: Đa-vít bảo thầy tế lễ A-bi-a-tha, con trai A-hi-mê-léc: "Xin đem áo ê-phót lại đây cho tôi." Vậy A-bi-a-tha đem áo ê-phót đến cho Đa-vít.
vi.R: Đa-vít nói với thầy tế lễ A-bi-a-tha, con trai A-hi-mê-léc: "Xin đem áo ê-phót đến cho tôi." Áo ê-phót là áo của thầy tế lễ, dùng để cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời. A-bi-a-tha đem áo ấy đến cho Đa-vít.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 아히멜렉의 아들 제사장 아비아달에게 말했다. "부디 에봇을 나에게 가까이 가져오십시오." 그러자 아비아달이 에봇을 다윗에게 가까이 가져왔다.
ko.B: 다윗이 아히멜렉의 아들 제사장 아비아달에게 말했다. "에봇을 저에게 가져오십시오." 아비아달은 에봇을 다윗에게 가져왔다.
ko.R: 다윗이 아히멜렉의 아들인 제사장 아비아달에게 말했다. "에봇을 가져와 주십시오." 에봇은 하나님께 답을 여쭐 때 쓰는 제사장의 조끼였다. 아비아달이 그것을 다윗에게 가져왔다.

decisions.choice: Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech: the one priest who escaped Saul's killing at Nob
decisions.reason: Saul had the priests of Nob put to death for helping David. Only Abiathar escaped and fled to David (22:20-23), and he brought an ephod with him (23:6).

decisions.choice: bring the ephod near: bring the priestly garment used to ask God's answer
decisions.reason: The ephod held the breastpiece with the Urim and Thummim, by which the LORD's will was asked (Exodus 28:6-30; Numbers 27:21; see 14:3). David asks through it here, as he did at Keilah (23:9-12).

decisions.choice: The ephod was the priest's vest used to ask God for answers.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as at 14:3.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֨ל דָּוִ֤ד בַּֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אֶרְדֹּ֛ף אַחֲרֵ֥י הַגְּדוּד־הַזֶּ֖ה הַֽאַשִּׂגֶ֑נּוּ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ רְדֹ֔ף כִּֽי־הַשֵּׂ֥ג תַּשִּׂ֖יג וְהַצֵּ֥ל תַּצִּֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: And inquired David of Yahweh, saying, Shall I pursue after the band the this? Will I overtake it? And he said to him, Pursue, for overtaking you will overtake and rescuing you will rescue.

en.L: And David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Shall I pursue after this band? Will I overtake it?" And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Pursue, for you will surely overtake [them], and you will surely rescue [them]."
en.B: Then David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Should I go after this raiding party? Will I catch up with them?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered him, "Go after them. You will certainly catch up with them, and you will certainly rescue the captives."
en.R: David asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Should I chase these raiders? Will I catch them?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Chase them. You will surely catch them, and you will surely save the people they took."

es.L: Y consultó David {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, diciendo: «¿Perseguiré a esta banda? ¿La alcanzaré?». Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le dijo: «Persíguela, porque de cierto [la] alcanzarás, y de cierto [los] librarás».
es.B: Entonces David consultó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¿Debo perseguir a esta banda de saqueadores? ¿Los alcanzaré?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió: «Persíguelos. Sin duda los alcanzarás, y sin duda rescatarás a los cautivos».
es.R: David le preguntó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¿Debo perseguir a estos saqueadores? ¿Los voy a alcanzar?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió: «Persíguelos. Sin duda los alcanzarás, y sin duda salvarás a la gente que se llevaron».

fr.L: Et David consulta {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, en disant : « Poursuivrai-je cette bande ? L’atteindrai-je ? » Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Poursuis, car tu [les] atteindras certainement, et tu [les] délivreras certainement. »
fr.B: Alors David consulta {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : « Dois-je poursuivre cette bande de pillards ? Vais-je les rattraper ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui répondit : « Poursuis-les. Tu les rattraperas sans faute, et tu délivreras sans faute les captifs. »
fr.R: David a demandé {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Est-ce que je dois poursuivre ces pillards ? Est-ce que je vais les attraper ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a répondu : « Poursuis-les. Tu vas sûrement les attraper, et tu vas sûrement sauver les gens qu’ils ont emmenés. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akisema, "Je, nikifuatie kikosi hiki? Je, nitakipata?" Naye akamwambia, "Fuatia, kwa maana hakika utawapata, na hakika utawaokoa."
sw.B: Kisha Daudi akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Je, nikifuatie kikosi hiki cha wavamizi? Je, nitawapata?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamjibu, "Wafuatie. Hakika utawapata, na hakika utawaokoa mateka."
sw.R: Daudi akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Je, niwafuatie wavamizi hawa? Je, nitawapata?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu, "Wafuatie. Hakika utawapata, na hakika utawaokoa watu waliowateka."

vi.L: Đa-vít cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rằng: "Con có nên đuổi theo toán quân này không? Con có đuổi kịp chúng không?" {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán với ông: "Hãy đuổi theo, vì ngươi chắc chắn sẽ đuổi kịp, và chắc chắn sẽ giải cứu được."
vi.B: Rồi Đa-vít cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Con có nên đuổi theo toán quân cướp này không? Con có đuổi kịp chúng không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Hãy đuổi theo chúng. Con chắc chắn sẽ đuổi kịp, và chắc chắn sẽ giải cứu được những người bị bắt."
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Con có nên đuổi theo bọn cướp này không? Con có bắt kịp chúng không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Hãy đuổi theo chúng. Con chắc chắn sẽ bắt kịp, và chắc chắn sẽ cứu được những người chúng đã bắt."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈어 말했다. "제가 이 무리를 뒤쫓아야 합니까? 제가 그들을 따라잡겠습니까?" 그러자 그분께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "뒤쫓아라. 네가 반드시 따라잡고 반드시 구해 낼 것이다."
ko.B: 다윗이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈었다. "제가 이 약탈대를 뒤쫓아야 합니까? 제가 그들을 따라잡을 수 있겠습니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "뒤쫓아라. 너는 반드시 그들을 따라잡고, 반드시 사로잡힌 사람들을 구해 낼 것이다."
ko.R: 다윗이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈었다. "제가 이 약탈자들을 쫓아가야 합니까? 제가 그들을 잡을 수 있겠습니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대답하셨다. "쫓아가거라. 너는 꼭 그들을 잡을 것이고, 그들이 끌고 간 사람들을 꼭 구해 낼 것이다."

decisions.choice: two questions that can be answered yes or no
decisions.reason: Asking the LORD through the ephod gave answers of this kind, so David puts his questions in that form (14:37; 23:11-12). The answer meets both questions: "Pursue" answers the first, and the promise answers the second.

decisions.choice: the band: a raiding troop that strikes and withdraws
decisions.reason: The word names a band of raiders rather than a regular army (verses 15, 23; 2 Samuel 3:22).

decisions.choice: overtaking you will overtake, rescuing you will rescue: a certain promise
decisions.reason: Each verb is doubled for emphasis: David will certainly catch up and certainly rescue. "Rescue" has no object here; it covers the captives and the goods, as verses 18-19 show.

decisions.choice: he said, with a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The one who answers is the LORD, so the pronoun takes the reader setting for pronouns referring to God.

decisions.choice: The LORD answered; the captives / the people they took
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker and say what will be rescued (m3).

decisions.choice: "Naye akamwambia" with no span
decisions.reason: The English Literal "he" for the LORD takes a deity pronoun span; Swahili "naye" is joined to "and" here and the subject is in the verb, so there is no free pronoun to capitalize.

source.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד ה֚וּאוְשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד־נַ֣חַל הַבְּשׂ֑וֹר וְהַנּֽוֹתָרִ֖ים עָמָֽדוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went David, he and six hundred men who [were] with him, and they came to [the] wadi of the Besor, and those left behind stayed.

en.L: And David went, he and the 600 men who [were] with him, and they came to the Wadi Besor, and those left behind stayed [there].
en.B: So David set out with the 600 men who were with him. They came to the Wadi Besor, where those who were left behind stayed.
en.R: So David left with his 600 men. They came to the Besor Valley. Some of the men stayed there.

es.L: Y fue David, él y los seiscientos hombres que [estaban] con él, y llegaron al arroyo de Besor, y los que se quedaron atrás permanecieron [allí].
es.B: Así que David se puso en marcha con los seiscientos hombres que estaban con él. Llegaron al arroyo de Besor, donde se quedaron los que no pudieron seguir.
es.R: Así que David salió con sus seiscientos hombres. Llegaron al valle de Besor. Algunos de los hombres se quedaron allí.

fr.L: Et David s’en alla, lui et les six cents hommes qui [étaient] avec lui, et ils arrivèrent au torrent de Bésor, et ceux qui restaient en arrière s’arrêtèrent [là].
fr.B: David partit donc avec les six cents hommes qui l’accompagnaient. Ils arrivèrent au torrent de Bésor, où s’arrêtèrent ceux qui restaient en arrière.
fr.R: Alors David est parti avec ses six cents hommes. Ils sont arrivés au ravin de Bésor. Certains des hommes sont restés là.

sw.L: Daudi akaenda, yeye na watu 600 waliokuwa pamoja naye, wakafika kwenye kijito cha Besori, na wale walioachwa nyuma wakakaa [huko].
sw.B: Basi Daudi akaondoka pamoja na watu 600 waliokuwa pamoja naye. Wakafika kwenye kijito cha Besori, mahali walipobaki wale walioachwa nyuma.
sw.R: Basi Daudi akaondoka pamoja na watu wake 600. Wakafika kwenye bonde la Besori. Baadhi ya watu wakabaki huko.

vi.L: Đa-vít ra đi, ông và 600 người ở với ông, và họ đến khe Bê-sô, nơi những người bị bỏ lại ở lại.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít lên đường cùng 600 người theo ông. Họ đến khe Bê-sô, là nơi những người bị bỏ lại ở lại.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít cùng 600 thuộc hạ lên đường. Họ đến thung lũng Bê-sô. Một số người ở lại đó.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗과 그와 함께 있던 육백 명이 가서 브솔 시내에 이르렀는데, 뒤에 남은 사람들은 [그곳에] 머물렀다.
ko.B: 다윗은 자기와 함께 있던 육백 명을 데리고 길을 떠나 브솔 시내에 이르렀다. 뒤처진 사람들은 그곳에 머물렀다.
ko.R: 다윗은 부하 육백 명과 함께 떠나서 브솔 골짜기에 이르렀다. 부하들 가운데 몇은 그곳에 남았다.

decisions.choice: the Wadi Besor: a streambed south of Ziklag
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley with a stream that runs only in the rainy season. The Besor runs from the Negev to the sea south of Gaza, and its banks are steep in places, which is why crossing it was hard for tired men (verse 10).

decisions.choice: those left behind stayed: a first word about what verse 10 tells in full
decisions.reason: The narrator mentions the men who stayed at the wadi before explaining who they were and why they stayed.

decisions.choice: the Besor Valley
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for the dry streambed (m1).

decisions.choice: le torrent de Bésor (L, B); le ravin de Bésor (R)
decisions.reason: French "torrent" names a stream that runs only in the rainy season (m1); Readable says "ravin", the dry valley, as the English "valley".

decisions.choice: el arroyo de Besor (L, B); el valle de Besor (R)
decisions.reason: A streambed south of Ziklag (m1), named with “arroyo” as the wadi of 17:40; Readable says “valle”, as the English Readable says “Besor Valley” (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: "kijito cha Besori" (L, B); "bonde la Besori" (R)
decisions.reason: A wadi is a streambed that runs only in the rains (m1); "kijito" (stream) at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says "bonde" (valley), as the English says "valley".

decisions.choice: "khe Bê-sô" (L, B); "thung lũng Bê-sô" (R)
decisions.reason: A wadi is a streambed that is dry most of the year (m1); "khe" says that better than "suối", and Readable follows the English "valley".

decisions.choice: "브솔 시내" (L, B) and "브솔 골짜기" (R) for the Wadi Besor
decisions.reason: A streambed, often dry (meaning decision m1); "시내" is the usual Korean word for such a wadi, and Readable says "valley" as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיִּרְדֹּ֣ף דָּוִ֔ד ה֖וּא וְאַרְבַּע־מֵא֣וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ מָאתַ֣יִם אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּגְּר֔וּ מֵעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת־נַ֥חַל הַבְּשֽׂוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And pursued David, he and four hundred man, and stayed two hundred man who were exhausted from crossing the wadi of the Besor.

en.L: And David pursued, he and 400 men, and 200 men who were too exhausted to cross the Wadi Besor stayed [behind].
en.B: David and 400 men kept up the pursuit, while 200 men stayed behind, too exhausted to cross the Wadi Besor.
en.R: David and 400 men kept chasing the Amalekites. But 200 men were too tired to cross the valley, so they stayed behind.

es.L: Y persiguió David, él y cuatrocientos hombres, y se quedaron doscientos hombres que estaban demasiado agotados para cruzar el arroyo de Besor.
es.B: David y cuatrocientos hombres siguieron la persecución, mientras doscientos se quedaron atrás, demasiado agotados para cruzar el arroyo de Besor.
es.R: David y cuatrocientos hombres siguieron persiguiendo a los amalecitas. Pero doscientos hombres estaban demasiado cansados para cruzar el valle, así que se quedaron atrás.

fr.L: Et David poursuivit, lui et quatre cents hommes, et deux cents hommes, trop épuisés pour traverser le torrent de Bésor, restèrent [en arrière].
fr.B: David et quatre cents hommes continuèrent la poursuite, tandis que deux cents hommes, trop épuisés pour traverser le torrent de Bésor, restèrent en arrière.
fr.R: David et quatre cents hommes ont continué à poursuivre les Amalécites. Mais deux cents hommes étaient trop fatigués pour traverser le ravin, alors ils sont restés en arrière.

sw.L: Daudi akafuatia, yeye na watu 400, na watu 200 waliochoka mno kuvuka kijito cha Besori wakakaa [nyuma].
sw.B: Daudi na watu 400 wakaendelea kufuatia, na watu 200 wakabaki nyuma, wakiwa wamechoka mno kuvuka kijito cha Besori.
sw.R: Daudi na watu 400 wakaendelea kuwafuatia Waamaleki. Lakini watu 200 walikuwa wamechoka sana kuvuka bonde hilo, kwa hiyo wakabaki nyuma.

vi.L: Đa-vít đuổi theo, ông và 400 người, còn 200 người quá mệt mỏi không thể qua khe Bê-sô thì ở lại.
vi.B: Đa-vít và 400 người tiếp tục đuổi theo, còn 200 người ở lại vì quá kiệt sức không thể vượt qua khe Bê-sô.
vi.R: Đa-vít và 400 người tiếp tục đuổi theo người A-ma-léc. Nhưng 200 người quá mệt, không vượt qua thung lũng được, nên họ ở lại.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗과 사백 명은 뒤쫓았고, 너무 지쳐서 브솔 시내를 건너지 못한 이백 명은 [뒤에] 머물렀다.
ko.B: 다윗은 사백 명과 함께 계속 뒤쫓았고, 너무 지쳐서 브솔 시내를 건널 수 없었던 이백 명은 뒤에 남았다.
ko.R: 다윗과 사백 명은 계속 아말렉 사람들을 쫓아갔다. 그러나 이백 명은 너무 지쳐서 골짜기를 건널 수 없었다. 그래서 그들은 뒤에 남았다.

decisions.choice: exhausted: too worn out to go on
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here and in verse 21. From the setting it means to be faint or spent. The men had marched for three days from Aphek (verse 1) and then wept until they had no strength left (verse 4).

decisions.choice: he and 400 men: David goes on with two thirds of his force
decisions.reason: The 600 of verse 9 are now divided: 400 go on, 200 stay. Verses 21-25 turn on the share of these 200.

decisions.choice: chasing the Amalekites
decisions.reason: Readable names whom David was pursuing.

source.text: וַֽיִּמְצְא֤וּ אִישׁ־מִצְרִי֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיִּקְח֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אֶל־דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּתְּנוּ־ל֥וֹ לֶ֨חֶם֙ וַיֹּ֔אכַל וַיַּשְׁקֻ֖הוּ מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they found a man, Egyptian, in the field, and they took him to David, and they gave to him bread and he ate, and they gave him to drink water.

en.L: And they found an Egyptian man in the open country, and they took him to David, and they gave him bread and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.
en.B: They found an Egyptian out in the open country and brought him to David. They gave him food to eat and water to drink.
en.R: David's men found a man from Egypt out in the fields. They brought him to David. They gave him some bread to eat and water to drink.

es.L: Y encontraron a un hombre egipcio en el campo, y lo llevaron a David, y le dieron pan y comió, y le dieron a beber agua.
es.B: Encontraron a un egipcio en el campo abierto y se lo llevaron a David. Le dieron de comer y de beber agua.
es.R: Los hombres de David encontraron a un hombre de Egipto en el campo. Lo llevaron ante David. Le dieron un poco de pan para comer y agua para beber.

fr.L: Et ils trouvèrent dans la campagne un homme égyptien, et ils l’emmenèrent à David, et ils lui donnèrent du pain, et il mangea, et ils lui donnèrent de l’eau à boire.
fr.B: Ils trouvèrent un Égyptien dans la campagne et l’amenèrent à David. Ils lui donnèrent à manger et à boire.
fr.R: Les hommes de David ont trouvé un Égyptien dans les champs. Ils l’ont amené à David. Ils lui ont donné du pain à manger et de l’eau à boire.

sw.L: Wakamkuta Mmisri mmoja shambani, wakamleta kwa Daudi, wakampa mkate, akala, wakamnywesha maji.
sw.B: Wakamkuta Mmisri mmoja nje porini, wakamleta kwa Daudi. Wakampa chakula akala, na maji akanywa.
sw.R: Watu wa Daudi wakamkuta mtu mmoja wa Misri huko porini. Wakamleta kwa Daudi. Wakampa mkate ale, na maji anywe.

vi.L: Họ gặp một người Ai Cập ngoài đồng, đem người ấy đến với Đa-vít, cho người ấy bánh và người ấy ăn, rồi cho người ấy uống nước.
vi.B: Họ gặp một người Ai Cập ngoài đồng trống và đem đến cho Đa-vít. Họ cho người ấy ăn bánh và uống nước.
vi.R: Thuộc hạ của Đa-vít gặp một người Ai Cập ngoài đồng. Họ dẫn người ấy đến với Đa-vít. Họ cho người ấy ăn bánh và uống nước.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 들에서 이집트 사람 하나를 찾아 다윗에게 데려왔다. 그리고 그들이 그에게 빵을 주어 먹게 하고, 물을 주어 마시게 했다.
ko.B: 그들은 들판에서 이집트 사람 하나를 발견하여 다윗에게 데려왔다. 그리고 그에게 먹을 것과 마실 물을 주었다.
ko.R: 다윗의 부하들은 들판에서 이집트 사람 하나를 발견했다. 그들은 그를 다윗에게 데려왔다. 그리고 그에게 빵과 물을 주어 먹고 마시게 했다.

decisions.choice: in the field: out in the open country
decisions.reason: The word means open land away from towns, whether pasture, farmland or wild ground.

decisions.choice: bread: food
decisions.reason: The word means bread and often food in general (verse 12).

decisions.choice: David's men
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are.

source.text: וַיִּתְּנוּ־לוֹ֩ פֶ֨לַח דְּבֵלָ֜ה וּשְׁנֵ֤י צִמֻּקִים֙ וַיֹּ֔אכַל וַתָּ֥שָׁב רוּח֖וֹ אֵלָ֑יו כִּ֠י לֹֽא־אָ֤כַל לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְלֹא־שָׁ֣תָה מַ֔יִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יָמִ֖ים וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה לֵילֽוֹת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they gave to him a piece of fig cake and two clusters of raisins, and he ate, and returned his spirit to him, for not he had eaten bread and not he had drunk water three days and three nights.

en.L: And they gave him a piece of fig cake and two clusters of raisins, and he ate, and his spirit returned to him, for he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights.
en.B: They also gave him a piece of pressed fig cake and two clusters of raisins. When he had eaten, his strength came back, for he had had no food or water for three days and three nights.
en.R: They gave him part of a cake of dried figs and two bunches of raisins. After he ate, he felt strong again. He had not eaten any food or drunk any water for three whole days and nights.

es.L: Y le dieron un pedazo de torta de higos y dos racimos de pasas, y comió, y le volvió el espíritu, porque no había comido pan ni bebido agua en tres días y tres noches.
es.B: También le dieron un pedazo de torta de higos y dos racimos de pasas. Cuando comió, recobró las fuerzas, porque llevaba tres días y tres noches sin comer ni beber.
es.R: Le dieron parte de una torta de higos secos y dos racimos de pasas. Después de comer, se sintió fuerte otra vez. No había comido nada ni bebido agua en tres días con sus noches.

fr.L: Et ils lui donnèrent un morceau de gâteau de figues et deux grappes de raisins secs, et il mangea, et son esprit lui revint, car il n’avait pas mangé de pain ni bu d’eau depuis trois jours et trois nuits.
fr.B: Ils lui donnèrent aussi un morceau de gâteau de figues et deux grappes de raisins secs. Quand il eut mangé, ses forces lui revinrent, car il n’avait rien mangé ni rien bu depuis trois jours et trois nuits.
fr.R: Ils lui ont donné un morceau de gâteau de figues sèches et deux grappes de raisins secs. Après avoir mangé, il a retrouvé des forces. Il n’avait rien mangé et rien bu depuis trois jours et trois nuits.

sw.L: Wakampa kipande cha andazi la tini na vishada viwili vya zabibu kavu, akala, roho yake ikamrudia, kwa maana hakuwa amekula mkate wala kunywa maji siku tatu, mchana na usiku.
sw.B: Wakampa pia kipande cha andazi la tini zilizoshindiliwa na vishada viwili vya zabibu kavu. Alipokwisha kula, nguvu zake zikamrudia, kwa maana hakuwa amekula wala kunywa kwa siku tatu, mchana na usiku.
sw.R: Wakampa kipande cha mkate wa tini zilizokaushwa na vishada viwili vya zabibu kavu. Alipokwisha kula, akajisikia mwenye nguvu tena. Hakuwa amekula chakula wala kunywa maji kwa siku tatu nzima, mchana na usiku.

vi.L: Họ cho người ấy một miếng bánh trái vả và hai chùm nho khô; người ấy ăn, và tâm thần người hồi lại, vì người đã không ăn bánh, không uống nước ba ngày ba đêm.
vi.B: Họ còn cho người ấy một miếng bánh trái vả ép và hai chùm nho khô. Ăn xong, người ấy hồi sức lại, vì đã ba ngày ba đêm không ăn không uống gì.
vi.R: Họ cho người ấy một miếng bánh trái vả khô và hai chùm nho khô. Ăn xong, người ấy thấy khỏe lại. Người ấy đã không ăn không uống gì suốt ba ngày ba đêm.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그에게 무화과 뭉치 한 조각과 건포도 두 송이를 주니, 그가 먹고 그의 기운이 그에게 돌아왔다. 그가 사흘 밤낮 동안 빵을 먹지 못하고 물을 마시지 못했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그들은 그에게 무화과 뭉치 한 조각과 건포도 두 송이도 주었다. 그가 먹고 나자 기운을 되찾았다. 그는 사흘 밤낮 동안 아무것도 먹지 못하고 물도 마시지 못했던 것이다.
ko.R: 그들은 그에게 말린 무화과 덩어리 한 조각과 건포도 두 송이를 주었다. 그는 먹고 나서 다시 기운을 차렸다. 그는 사흘 밤낮 동안 아무것도 먹지 못하고 물도 마시지 못했었다.

decisions.choice: fig cake and clusters of raisins: dried fruit pressed for travel
decisions.reason: Figs were pressed into cakes and grapes dried in clusters, food that kept and could be carried. Abigail brought the same things to David (25:18).

decisions.choice: his spirit returned to him: his strength and alertness came back
decisions.reason: "Spirit" here is breath and life-force. The same phrase is used of Samson when he drinks after the battle (Judges 15:19).

decisions.choice: his strength came back; he felt strong again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֤וֹ דָוִד֙ לְֽמִי־אַ֔תָּה וְאֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּ֜אמֶר נַ֧עַר מִצְרִ֣י אָנֹ֗כִי עֶ֚בֶד לְאִ֣ישׁ עֲמָֽלֵקִ֔י וַיַּעַזְבֵ֧נִי אֲדֹנִ֛י כִּ֥י חָלִ֖יתִי הַיּ֥וֹם שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him David, To whom [are] you, and where from this [are] you? And he said, [A] young man, Egyptian, [am] I, [a] slave of a man, Amalekite, and abandoned me my master, for I was sick the day three.

en.L: And David said to him, "To whom [do] you [belong], and where [are] you from?" And he said, "I [am] a young Egyptian man, [the] slave of an Amalekite man, and my master abandoned me, because I fell sick three days ago.
en.B: David asked him, "Who do you belong to, and where are you from?" He answered, "I am a young Egyptian, the servant of an Amalekite. My master left me behind three days ago because I fell sick.
en.R: David asked him, "Who is your master? Where are you from?" He said, "I am from Egypt. I am the servant of an Amalekite man. Three days ago I got sick, so my master left me behind.

es.L: Y le dijo David: «¿De quién [eres] tú, y de dónde [eres]?». Y él dijo: «Yo [soy] un joven egipcio, esclavo de un hombre amalecita, y mi amo me abandonó, porque enfermé hace tres días.
es.B: David le preguntó: «¿A quién perteneces, y de dónde eres?». Él respondió: «Soy un joven egipcio, siervo de un amalecita. Mi amo me dejó atrás hace tres días porque me enfermé.
es.R: David le preguntó: «¿Quién es tu amo? ¿De dónde eres?». Él dijo: «Soy de Egipto. Soy siervo de un hombre amalecita. Hace tres días me enfermé, y mi amo me dejó atrás.

fr.L: Et David lui dit : « À qui [es]-tu, et d’où [es]-tu ? » Et il dit : « Je [suis] un jeune Égyptien, l’esclave d’un homme amalécite, et mon maître m’a abandonné parce que je suis tombé malade il y a trois jours.

decisions.choice: to whom are you: whose man are you
decisions.reason: The question asks whom he belongs to: his master, his clan or his people. His answer names both his people and his master.

decisions.choice: slave of an Amalekite: owned, and abandoned when he was no longer useful
decisions.reason: He was not hired but owned, and his master left him to die when he fell sick and could not keep up with the raiders.

decisions.choice: the day three: three days ago
decisions.reason: Counting the present day, this means the day before yesterday, which fits the three days and nights he had gone without food (verse 12).

decisions.choice: servant (Balanced and Readable); slave (Literal)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for this word: Literal keeps "slave"; Balanced and Readable say "servant", while m2 keeps the fact that he was owned.

decisions.choice: David says "ngươi" to the Egyptian; he answers with "tôi" and "ông"
decisions.reason: A leader questioning a captured slave of the enemy; the slave speaks up to him.

decisions.choice: David speaks to the Egyptian in the plain style (해라체); he answers in the formal polite style (합쇼체); "종" for slave at every level
decisions.reason: A commander questioning a captive; Korean "종" covers both "slave" and "servant", so the English split between levels has no Korean counterpart here.

decisions.choice: the Negev of the Cherethites: southern land held by a people linked with the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Cherethites lived near the Philistines on the southern coast (Ezekiel 25:16; Zephaniah 2:5) and probably came from Crete. Later some of them served as David's guard (2 Samuel 8:18).

decisions.choice: what belongs to Judah: the Negev of Judah
decisions.reason: The phrase stands for the southern land of Judah, which David named in his reports to Achish (27:10).

decisions.choice: the Negev of Caleb: the southern land of the clan of Caleb
decisions.reason: Caleb was given Hebron and the land around it (Joshua 14:13; 15:13), and his clan lived there and to the south. Nabal was a Calebite (25:3).

decisions.choice: the land of ...; Caleb's people
decisions.reason: Readable says "the south" once and then "the land of" for each part, and makes clear that Caleb here means his clan.

decisions.choice: los cereteos; el Néguev
decisions.reason: A southern people linked with the Philistines (m1), in the usual Spanish form; “Néguev” with its accent, as in 27:10.

decisions.choice: "Wakerethi"; "Negebu" (L, B), "upande wa kusini" (R)
decisions.reason: Peoples take the prefix wa-; "Negebu" is kept at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says "the south", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "người Kê-rê-thít"; "Ca-lép"
decisions.reason: Names not in the terms note's table, in the usual Protestant forms.

decisions.choice: "그렛 사람들", "갈렙"
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant Korean forms; the Cherethites are a people linked with the Philistines (meaning decision m1).

records.literal_gloss: And said to him David, Will you bring me down to the band the this? And he said, Swear to me by God, if you will kill me and if you will deliver me into [the] hand of my master, and I will bring you down to the band the this.

en.L: And David said to him, "Will you take me down to this band?" And he said, "Swear to me by God that you will not kill me and will not hand me over into the hand of my master, and I will take you down to this band."
en.B: David asked him, "Will you lead me down to this raiding party?" He replied, "Give me your oath by God that you will neither kill me nor hand me over to my master, and I will take you down to them."
en.R: David asked, "Can you lead me to these raiders?" He answered, "Promise me in God's name that you will not kill me or give me back to my master. Then I will take you to them."

es.L: Y le dijo David: «¿Me llevarás a esa banda?». Y él dijo: «Júrame por Dios que no me matarás ni me entregarás en mano de mi amo, y yo te llevaré a esa banda».
es.B: David le preguntó: «¿Puedes guiarme hasta esa banda de saqueadores?». Él respondió: «Júrame por Dios que no me matarás ni me entregarás a mi amo, y te llevaré hasta ellos».
es.R: David le preguntó: «¿Puedes llevarme a donde están esos saqueadores?». Él le contestó: «Prométeme en el nombre de Dios que no me matarás ni me devolverás a mi amo. Entonces te llevaré hasta ellos».

fr.L: Et David lui dit : « Me feras-tu descendre vers cette bande ? » Et il dit : « Jure-moi par Dieu que tu ne me tueras pas et que tu ne me livreras pas dans la main de mon maître, et je te ferai descendre vers cette bande. »
fr.B: David lui demanda : « Veux-tu me conduire jusqu’à cette bande ? » Il répondit : « Jure-moi par Dieu que tu ne me tueras pas et que tu ne me livreras pas à mon maître, et je te conduirai jusqu’à eux. »
fr.R: David lui a demandé : « Est-ce que tu peux me conduire jusqu’à ces pillards ? » Il a répondu : « Promets-moi au nom de Dieu que tu ne me tueras pas et que tu ne me rendras pas à mon maître. Alors je te conduirai jusqu’à eux. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia, "Je, utanishusha kwa kikosi hiki?" Akasema, "Niapie kwa Mungu kwamba hutaniua, wala hutanitia mkononi mwa bwana wangu, nami nitakushusha kwa kikosi hiki."
sw.B: Daudi akamwuliza, "Je, utaniongoza mpaka kwa kikosi hiki cha wavamizi?" Akajibu, "Niapie kwa Mungu kwamba hutaniua wala kunitia mikononi mwa bwana wangu, nami nitakupeleka kwao."
sw.R: Daudi akauliza, "Unaweza kunipeleka mpaka kwa wavamizi hawa?" Akajibu, "Niahidi kwa jina la Mungu kwamba hutaniua wala kunirudisha kwa bwana wangu. Ndipo nitakupeleka kwao."

vi.L: Đa-vít hỏi người ấy: "Ngươi có dẫn ta xuống chỗ toán quân này không?" Người ấy nói: "Xin ông nhân danh Đức Chúa Trời thề với tôi rằng ông sẽ không giết tôi, và sẽ không nộp tôi vào tay chủ tôi, thì tôi sẽ dẫn ông xuống chỗ toán quân ấy."
vi.B: Đa-vít hỏi người ấy: "Ngươi có thể dẫn ta xuống chỗ toán quân cướp ấy không?" Người ấy đáp: "Xin ông nhân danh Đức Chúa Trời thề với tôi rằng ông sẽ không giết tôi cũng không nộp tôi cho chủ tôi, thì tôi sẽ dẫn ông xuống chỗ chúng."
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi: "Ngươi có thể dẫn ta đến chỗ bọn cướp ấy không?" Người ấy đáp: "Xin ông nhân danh Đức Chúa Trời hứa với tôi là ông sẽ không giết tôi hay trả tôi về cho chủ tôi. Rồi tôi sẽ dẫn ông đến chỗ chúng."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 그에게 말했다. "너는 나를 이 무리에게로 데리고 내려가겠느냐?" 그러자 그가 말했다. "당신이 저를 죽이지도 않고 제 주인의 손에 넘기지도 않겠다고 하나님을 두고 저에게 맹세해 주십시오. 그러면 제가 당신을 이 무리에게로 데리고 내려가겠습니다."
ko.B: 다윗이 그에게 물었다. "너는 나를 그 약탈대가 있는 곳으로 데려가 줄 수 있느냐?" 그가 대답했다. "저를 죽이지도 않고 제 주인에게 넘기지도 않겠다고 하나님의 이름으로 맹세해 주십시오. 그러면 그들이 있는 곳으로 모시고 가겠습니다."
ko.R: 다윗이 물었다. "그 약탈자들이 있는 곳으로 나를 데려갈 수 있느냐?" 그가 대답했다. "저를 죽이지 않고 제 주인에게 돌려보내지도 않겠다고 하나님의 이름으로 약속해 주십시오. 그러면 그들에게 모시고 가겠습니다."

decisions.choice: swear ... if you kill me: swear that you will not kill me
decisions.reason: In an oath, "if" with no second half means "certainly not": "may it happen to me if I do." So he asks for a promise that David will neither kill him nor return him.

decisions.choice: swear by God: an oath in the name of God
decisions.reason: The Egyptian uses the general word for God, not the LORD's name. An oath in God's name bound the one who swore before God.

decisions.choice: deliver into the hand of my master: hand me over to his power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power or control. A runaway slave returned to his master could expect harsh treatment.

decisions.choice: to them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid repeating "this band" at the end of the sentence.
