records.literal_gloss: And he brought him down, and there! [they were] spread out over [the] face of all the land, eating and drinking and celebrating, because of all the plunder the great which they had taken from [the] land of [the] Philistines and from [the] land of Judah.

en.L: And he took him down, and look, they [were] spread out over the face of all the land, eating and drinking and celebrating, because of all the great plunder that they had taken from the land of [the] Philistines and from the land of Judah.
en.B: So he led him down, and there they were, spread out over the whole area, eating and drinking and celebrating over all the great plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
en.R: So the Egyptian led David down to them. The Amalekites were scattered all over the place. They were eating and drinking and having a party. They were celebrating all the things they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from Judah.

es.L: Y lo llevó, y he aquí que ellos [estaban] desparramados sobre la faz de toda la tierra, comiendo, bebiendo y festejando por todo el gran botín que habían tomado de la tierra de los filisteos y de la tierra de Judá.
es.B: Así que lo guió hasta allá, y allí estaban, desparramados por toda la zona, comiendo, bebiendo y festejando por el gran botín que habían tomado de la tierra de los filisteos y de la tierra de Judá.
es.R: Así que el egipcio llevó a David hasta donde estaban. Los amalecitas estaban dispersos por todas partes. Estaban comiendo, bebiendo y haciendo fiesta. Celebraban por todas las cosas que habían robado de la tierra de los filisteos y de Judá.

fr.L: Et il le fit descendre, et voici, ils [étaient] répandus sur la face de tout le pays, mangeant, et buvant, et faisant la fête, à cause de tout le grand butin qu’ils avaient pris au pays des Philistins et au pays de Juda.
fr.B: Il l’y conduisit, et voici qu’ils étaient dispersés sur toute la région, à manger, à boire et à faire la fête, à cause de l’énorme butin qu’ils avaient pris au pays des Philistins et au pays de Juda.
fr.R: Alors l’Égyptien a conduit David jusqu’à eux. Les Amalécites étaient dispersés partout. Ils mangeaient, ils buvaient et ils faisaient la fête. Ils fêtaient toutes les choses qu’ils avaient prises au pays des Philistins et en Juda.

sw.L: Akamshusha, na tazama, walikuwa wametawanyika juu ya uso wa nchi yote, wakila na kunywa na kufanya sikukuu, kwa sababu ya nyara zote nyingi walizochukua kutoka nchi ya Wafilisti na kutoka nchi ya Yuda.
sw.B: Basi akamwongoza mpaka huko, na hao walikuwa wametawanyika katika eneo lote, wakila, wakinywa na kusherehekea kwa sababu ya nyara nyingi walizoteka kutoka nchi ya Wafilisti na kutoka nchi ya Yuda.
sw.R: Basi yule Mmisri akamwongoza Daudi mpaka kwao. Waamaleki walikuwa wametawanyika kila mahali. Walikuwa wakila, wakinywa na kufanya sherehe. Walikuwa wakisherehekea vitu vyote walivyoteka kutoka nchi ya Wafilisti na kutoka Yuda.

vi.L: Người ấy dẫn ông xuống, và kìa, chúng tràn ra khắp mặt đất, ăn uống và nhảy múa, vì mọi chiến lợi phẩm lớn chúng đã lấy được từ xứ Phi-li-tin và từ xứ Giu-đa.
vi.B: Vậy người ấy dẫn ông xuống, và kìa, chúng tản ra khắp vùng, ăn uống và vui chơi mừng số chiến lợi phẩm lớn chúng đã cướp được từ xứ Phi-li-tin và xứ Giu-đa.
vi.R: Vậy người Ai Cập dẫn Đa-vít xuống chỗ chúng. Người A-ma-léc đang tản ra khắp nơi. Chúng đang ăn uống và tiệc tùng. Chúng mừng vì những thứ chúng đã cướp được từ xứ Phi-li-tin và từ Giu-đa.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 그를 데리고 내려가니, 보라, 그들이 온 땅에 퍼져서 먹고 마시며 춤추고 있었다. 그들이 블레셋 사람들의 땅과 유다 땅에서 빼앗은 많은 전리품 때문이었다.
ko.B: 그가 다윗을 데리고 내려가 보니, 그들은 온 들판에 흩어져서 먹고 마시며 춤추고 있었다. 블레셋 땅과 유다 땅에서 빼앗아 온 엄청난 전리품을 두고 잔치를 벌이고 있었던 것이다.
ko.R: 그 이집트 사람이 다윗을 그들에게 데려갔다. 아말렉 사람들은 사방에 흩어져 있었다. 그들은 먹고 마시며 잔치를 벌이고 있었다. 블레셋 땅과 유다에서 빼앗아 온 물건들을 두고 즐거워하고 있었다.

decisions.choice: look, spread out: the raiders scattered and off guard
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, "look" shows the scene as the newcomers saw it. The raiders were spread over the whole area, not set in any guarded camp. They thought themselves safe, which gave David his chance.

decisions.choice: celebrating: feasting as at a festival, with dancing
decisions.reason: The verb is used for keeping a religious festival, and for dancing and making merry (Exodus 5:1, of holding a festival to the LORD in the wilderness).

decisions.choice: plunder from the land of the Philistines and of Judah
decisions.reason: The raid struck both peoples while their armies were away in the north at Aphek (29:1). The plunder from the Philistines is the reason David can later send some to Judah (verse 26).

decisions.choice: the Egyptian, David, the Amalekites
decisions.reason: Readable names the people behind each "he" and "they".

source.text: וַיַּכֵּ֥ם דָּוִ֛ד מֵהַנֶּ֥שֶׁף וְעַד־הָעֶ֖רֶב לְמָֽחֳרָתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־נִמְלַ֤ט מֵהֶם֙ אִ֔ישׁ כִּי֩ אִם־אַרְבַּ֨ע מֵא֧וֹת אִֽישׁ־נַ֛עַר אֲשֶׁר־רָכְב֥וּ עַל־הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים וַיָּנֻֽסוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And struck them David from the twilight and until the evening of their next day, and not escaped of them a man, except four hundred man [of] young men who rode on the camels and fled.

en.L: And David struck them from the twilight until the evening of their next day, and not a man of them escaped, except 400 young men who rode on the camels and fled.
en.B: From twilight until the evening of the following day David struck them down. Not one of them escaped except 400 young men, who got on camels and fled.
en.R: David attacked them from twilight until the evening of the next day. None of them got away except 400 young men. They got on camels and rode away.

es.L: Y los hirió David desde el crepúsculo hasta la tarde del día siguiente, y no escapó de ellos ningún hombre, salvo cuatrocientos jóvenes que montaron en los camellos y huyeron.
es.B: Desde el crepúsculo hasta la tarde del día siguiente David los fue abatiendo. No escapó ninguno de ellos, aparte de cuatrocientos jóvenes que montaron en camellos y huyeron.
es.R: David los atacó desde el anochecer hasta la tarde del día siguiente. Ninguno de ellos escapó, aparte de cuatrocientos jóvenes. Estos montaron en camellos y huyeron.

fr.L: Et David les frappa depuis le crépuscule jusqu’au soir de leur lendemain, et aucun d’eux n’échappa, sauf quatre cents jeunes gens qui montèrent sur les chameaux et s’enfuirent.
fr.B: Depuis le crépuscule jusqu’au soir du lendemain, David les tailla en pièces. Aucun d’eux n’échappa, sauf quatre cents jeunes gens qui montèrent sur des chameaux et s’enfuirent.
fr.R: David les a attaqués depuis le crépuscule jusqu’au soir du lendemain. Aucun d’eux ne s’est échappé, sauf quatre cents jeunes gens. Ils sont montés sur des chameaux et ils se sont enfuis.

sw.L: Daudi akawapiga tangu giza la jioni mpaka jioni ya siku yao iliyofuata, wala hakuokoka mtu hata mmoja wao, ila vijana 400 waliopanda ngamia, wakakimbia.
sw.B: Tangu mapambazuko ya giza mpaka jioni ya siku iliyofuata Daudi akawapiga. Hakuna hata mmoja wao aliyeokoka isipokuwa vijana 400 waliopanda ngamia, wakakimbia.
sw.R: Daudi akawashambulia tangu giza la jioni mpaka jioni ya siku iliyofuata. Hakuna hata mmoja wao aliyeokoka isipokuwa vijana 400. Hao walipanda ngamia wakakimbia.

vi.L: Đa-vít đánh chúng từ lúc chạng vạng cho đến chiều tối ngày hôm sau; không một người nào trong chúng thoát được, ngoại trừ 400 thanh niên cưỡi lạc đà chạy trốn.
vi.B: Đa-vít đánh chúng từ lúc chạng vạng cho đến chiều tối hôm sau. Không ai trong chúng thoát được, ngoại trừ 400 thanh niên cưỡi lạc đà chạy trốn.
vi.R: Đa-vít tấn công chúng từ lúc chạng vạng cho đến chiều tối hôm sau. Không ai thoát được, trừ 400 thanh niên. Họ cưỡi lạc đà chạy trốn.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 어스름부터 그 이튿날 저녁까지 그들을 쳤다. 낙타를 타고 도망친 젊은이 사백 명 말고는 그들 가운데 한 사람도 피하지 못했다.
ko.B: 다윗은 해 질 녘부터 이튿날 저녁까지 그들을 쳤다. 낙타를 타고 달아난 젊은이 사백 명 말고는 그들 가운데 한 사람도 살아남지 못했다.
ko.R: 다윗은 해 질 무렵부터 다음 날 저녁까지 그들을 공격했다. 젊은이 사백 명 말고는 아무도 도망치지 못했다. 그 사백 명은 낙타를 타고 달아났다.

decisions.choice: from the twilight until the evening of the next day: a fight lasting about a day
alternatives: from dawn until the evening of the next day
decisions.reason: The word for twilight is used both of the half-light of evening (Isaiah 5:11) and of dawn (Job 7:4). If it is evening twilight here, David attacked at dusk and fought until the next evening; if dawn, he attacked at first light and fought until the following evening. "Their next day" means the day after for the Amalekites.

decisions.choice: rode on the camels and fled: desert raiders escaping on fast mounts
decisions.reason: Desert raiders such as the Amalekites and Midianites came on camels (Judges 6:5; 7:12), and camels could outrun men on foot. The 400 who escape match the 400 men with David.

decisions.choice: twilight
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep "twilight", which, like the Hebrew word, can be evening or morning (m1).

decisions.choice: "giza la jioni" (L, R); "mapambazuko ya giza" (B)
decisions.reason: The twilight word can be evening or dawn (m1); Swahili has no single word for both, so Literal and Readable take evening twilight and Balanced the dim light before dawn. A reviewer may prefer one choice at every level.

decisions.choice: "어스름" (L) and "해 질 녘" / "해 질 무렵" (B, R) for the Hebrew twilight
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word can mean dusk or dawn; with "until the evening of the next day" most read it as dusk, the fight lasting about a day (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the neutral "어스름".

source.text: וַיַּצֵּ֣ל דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֖וּ עֲמָלֵ֑ק וְאֶת־שְׁתֵּ֥י נָשָׁ֖יו הִצִּ֥יל דָּוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And rescued David all that had taken Amalek, and his two wives rescued David.

en.L: And David rescued all that Amalek had taken, and David rescued his two wives.
en.B: David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, and he rescued his two wives.
en.R: David got back everything the Amalekites had taken. He also rescued his two wives.

es.L: Y rescató David todo lo que Amalec había tomado, y David rescató a sus dos mujeres.
es.B: David recuperó todo lo que los amalecitas se habían llevado, y rescató a sus dos esposas.
es.R: David recuperó todo lo que los amalecitas se habían llevado. También rescató a sus dos esposas.

fr.L: Et David délivra tout ce qu’Amalek avait pris, et David délivra ses deux femmes.
fr.B: David reprit tout ce que les Amalécites avaient emporté, et il délivra ses deux femmes.
fr.R: David a récupéré tout ce que les Amalécites avaient pris. Il a aussi délivré ses deux femmes.

sw.L: Daudi akaokoa vyote alivyochukua Amaleki, naye Daudi akawaokoa wake zake wawili.
sw.B: Daudi akavirudisha vyote ambavyo Waamaleki walikuwa wamechukua, akawaokoa pia wake zake wawili.
sw.R: Daudi akarudisha kila kitu ambacho Waamaleki walikuwa wamechukua. Akawaokoa pia wake zake wawili.

vi.L: Đa-vít giải cứu mọi thứ A-ma-léc đã lấy, và Đa-vít giải cứu hai vợ mình.
vi.B: Đa-vít thu hồi mọi thứ người A-ma-léc đã cướp, và ông cũng giải cứu được hai vợ mình.
vi.R: Đa-vít lấy lại tất cả những gì người A-ma-léc đã cướp. Ông cũng cứu được hai vợ mình.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 아말렉이 빼앗아 간 모든 것을 되찾았고, 다윗이 그의 두 아내도 구해 냈다.
ko.B: 다윗은 아말렉 사람들이 빼앗아 간 것을 모두 되찾았고, 두 아내도 구해 냈다.
ko.R: 다윗은 아말렉 사람들이 가져간 것을 모두 되찾았다. 두 아내도 구해 냈다.

decisions.choice: rescued: snatched back, recovered
decisions.reason: The verb means to snatch someone or something out of another's power. It is the word of the LORD's promise in verse 8, now kept.

decisions.choice: Amalek: the people of Amalek
decisions.reason: The name of the ancestor stands for the whole people (15:2-3; Exodus 17:8).

decisions.choice: his two wives David rescued: the wives named for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "his two wives" first in its clause, giving weight to the rescue of the women named in verse 5.

decisions.choice: the Amalekites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the name of the people (m2).

source.text: וְלֹ֣א נֶעְדַּר־לָ֠הֶם מִן־הַקָּטֹ֨ן וְעַד־הַגָּד֜וֹל וְעַד־בָּנִ֤ים וּבָנוֹת֙ וּמִשָּׁלָ֔ל וְעַ֛ד כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם הַכֹּ֖ל הֵשִׁ֥יב דָּוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And not was missing to them from the small and unto the great and unto sons and daughters and from plunder and unto all that they had taken for themselves; the all brought back David.

en.L: And nothing of theirs was missing, from the small to the great, to sons and daughters, and from [the] plunder to all that they had taken for themselves; David brought back everything.
en.B: Nothing of theirs was missing, small or great, sons or daughters, plunder or anything else the raiders had taken. David brought it all back.
en.R: Nothing was missing, large or small. David brought back every son and daughter, and everything else the raiders had taken.

es.L: Y no les faltó nada, desde el pequeño hasta el grande, hasta hijos e hijas, y desde el botín hasta todo lo que se habían llevado; todo lo recuperó David.
es.B: No les faltó nada, ni pequeño ni grande, ni hijos ni hijas, ni el botín ni nada de lo que los saqueadores se habían llevado. David lo recuperó todo.
es.R: No faltó nada, ni grande ni pequeño. David trajo de vuelta a todos los hijos y las hijas, y todo lo demás que los saqueadores se habían llevado.

fr.L: Et rien ne leur manqua, du petit au grand, jusqu’aux fils et aux filles, et depuis le butin jusqu’à tout ce qu’ils avaient pris pour eux ; David ramena tout.
fr.B: Rien ne leur manquait, ni petit ni grand, ni fils ni filles, ni rien du butin que les pillards avaient emporté. David ramena tout.
fr.R: Il ne manquait rien, ni de petit ni de grand. David a ramené tous les fils et toutes les filles, et tout ce que les pillards avaient pris.

sw.L: Wala hakuna kitu chao kilichopotea, kidogo wala kikubwa, wala wana wala binti, wala katika nyara, wala chochote walichojitwalia; Daudi akavirudisha vyote.
sw.B: Hakuna kitu chao kilichopotea, kidogo wala kikubwa, wana wala binti, nyara wala kitu kingine chochote ambacho wavamizi walikuwa wamechukua. Daudi akarudisha vyote.
sw.R: Hakuna kilichopotea, kikubwa wala kidogo. Daudi akarudisha kila mwana na binti, na kila kitu kingine ambacho wavamizi walikuwa wamechukua.

vi.L: Họ không mất gì cả, từ nhỏ đến lớn, đến con trai con gái, từ chiến lợi phẩm đến mọi thứ chúng đã lấy cho mình; Đa-vít đem về tất cả.
vi.B: Họ không mất thứ gì, dù nhỏ hay lớn, con trai hay con gái, chiến lợi phẩm hay bất cứ thứ gì bọn cướp đã lấy. Đa-vít đem về tất cả.
vi.R: Không mất thứ gì, dù lớn hay nhỏ. Đa-vít đem về mọi đứa con trai, con gái, và mọi thứ khác bọn cướp đã lấy.

ko.L: 그리고 작은 것부터 큰 것까지, 아들들과 딸들까지, 전리품부터 그들이 빼앗아 간 모든 것까지, 그들에게서 없어진 것이 하나도 없었다. 다윗이 모든 것을 되찾아 왔다.
ko.B: 작은 것이든 큰 것이든, 아들이든 딸이든, 전리품이든 약탈자들이 빼앗아 간 그 밖의 무엇이든, 없어진 것은 하나도 없었다. 다윗이 모두 되찾아 왔다.
ko.R: 크든 작든 없어진 것은 하나도 없었다. 다윗은 아들과 딸들을 모두 되찾았고, 약탈자들이 가져간 다른 것들도 모두 되찾아 왔다.

decisions.choice: from the small to the great: everything, of every kind
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the pair means "all of it". Here it covers people and goods alike, and the list goes on to children and plunder.

decisions.choice: nothing missing; David brought back everything
decisions.reason: The verse stresses that the promise of verse 8 was kept in full: the LORD had said David would rescue, and not one person or thing was lost.

decisions.choice: the raiders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "they" are, since "they" in the first clause are David's men.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח דָּוִ֔ד אֶת־כָּל־הַצֹּ֖אן וְהַבָּקָ֑ר נָהֲג֗וּ לִפְנֵי֙ הַמִּקְנֶ֣ה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ זֶ֖ה שְׁלַ֥ל דָּוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And took David all the flocks and the herds; they drove before the livestock the that, and they said, This [is the] plunder of David.

en.L: And David took all the flocks and the herds; they drove [them] before that livestock, and they said, "This [is] David's plunder."
en.B: David also took all the flocks and herds. His men drove them ahead of the other livestock and said, "This is David's plunder."
en.R: David also took all the Amalekites' sheep and cattle. His men drove these animals in front of the others and said, "This is David's plunder!"

es.L: Y tomó David todas las ovejas y las vacas; las arreaban delante de aquel ganado, y decían: «Este [es] el botín de David».
es.B: David también tomó todas las ovejas y las vacas. Sus hombres las arreaban delante del resto del ganado y decían: «Este es el botín de David».
es.R: David también tomó todas las ovejas y las vacas de los amalecitas. Sus hombres arreaban estos animales delante de los demás y decían: «¡Este es el botín de David!».

fr.L: Et David prit tout le petit et le gros bétail ; ils [le] conduisaient devant ce troupeau-là, et ils disaient : « Ceci [est] le butin de David. »
fr.B: David prit aussi tout le petit et le gros bétail. Ses hommes le firent marcher en tête du reste du troupeau en disant : « Voici le butin de David. »
fr.R: David a aussi pris tous les moutons et tous les bœufs des Amalécites. Ses hommes ont fait marcher ces bêtes devant les autres, en disant : « C’est le butin de David ! »

sw.L: Daudi akachukua kondoo wote na ng'ombe wote; wakawaswaga mbele ya mifugo ile, wakasema, "Hizi [ni] nyara za Daudi."
sw.B: Daudi akachukua pia kondoo wote na ng'ombe wote. Watu wake wakawaswaga mbele ya mifugo mingine, wakasema, "Hizi ni nyara za Daudi."
sw.R: Daudi akachukua pia kondoo wote na ng'ombe wote wa Waamaleki. Watu wake wakawaswaga wanyama hao mbele ya wale wengine, wakasema, "Hizi ni nyara za Daudi!"

vi.L: Đa-vít lấy tất cả các bầy chiên và bầy bò; họ lùa [chúng] đi trước đàn gia súc kia và nói: "Đây [là] chiến lợi phẩm của Đa-vít."
vi.B: Đa-vít cũng lấy tất cả các bầy chiên và bầy bò. Thuộc hạ ông lùa chúng đi trước các gia súc khác và nói: "Đây là chiến lợi phẩm của Đa-vít."
vi.R: Đa-vít cũng lấy tất cả chiên và bò của người A-ma-léc. Thuộc hạ của ông lùa những con vật ấy đi trước các con vật khác và nói: "Đây là chiến lợi phẩm của Đa-vít!"

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 양 떼와 소 떼를 모두 차지했다. 그들이 그 가축들 앞에서 [그것들을] 몰고 가며 말했다. "이것은 다윗의 전리품이다."
ko.B: 다윗은 양 떼와 소 떼도 모두 차지했다. 그의 부하들은 그 짐승들을 다른 가축들 앞에 몰고 가며 말했다. "이것은 다윗의 전리품이다."
ko.R: 다윗은 아말렉 사람들의 양과 소도 모두 차지했다. 그의 부하들은 이 짐승들을 다른 가축들 앞에 몰고 가면서 "이것은 다윗의 전리품이다!" 하고 외쳤다.

decisions.choice: David took the Amalekites' own flocks and herds; the men drove them ahead of the recovered animals
alternatives: the men drove all the livestock in front of David and said, "This is David's plunder"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief and hard to follow. The most likely sense is that, besides recovering what had been taken from Ziklag, David took the raiders' own flocks and herds, and his men drove these in front of the other livestock as David's prize. Another way to read it is that the men drove all the animals in front of David, calling the whole herd his plunder.

decisions.choice: This is David's plunder: the men honor David as their leader
decisions.reason: The cry gives the credit for the victory to David. In verse 26 David gives part of this plunder away to the elders of Judah.

decisions.choice: His men; the other livestock; the Amalekites' (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who drove the animals and which animals, following m1.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א דָוִ֗ד אֶל־מָאתַ֨יִם הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים אֲשֶֽׁר־פִּגְּר֣וּ׀מִלֶּ֣כֶת׀אַחֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד וַיֹּֽשִׁיבֻם֙ בְּנַ֣חַל הַבְּשׂ֔וֹר וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֔ד וְלִקְרַ֖את הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֤שׁ דָּוִד֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁאַ֥ל לָהֶ֖ם לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And came David to [the] two hundred the men who had been exhausted from going after David, and they had made them stay at [the] wadi of the Besor, and they went out to meet David and to meet the people who [were] with him; and approached David the people and asked them of peace.

en.L: And David came to the 200 men who had been too exhausted to go after David, whom they had left at the Wadi Besor; and they went out to meet David and to meet the people who [were] with him. And David approached the people and asked them about [their] well-being.
en.B: Then David came back to the 200 men who had been too exhausted to follow him and had been left at the Wadi Besor. They came out to meet David and the troops with him, and as David came near, he greeted them.
en.R: David came back to the 200 men who had been too tired to go with him. They had stayed at the Besor Valley. They came out to meet David and the soldiers with him. David went up to them and greeted them warmly.

es.L: Y llegó David a los doscientos hombres que habían estado demasiado agotados para seguir a David, a los que habían dejado en el arroyo de Besor; y salieron al encuentro de David y al encuentro del pueblo que [estaba] con él. Y se acercó David al pueblo y les preguntó por [su] bienestar.
es.B: Luego David volvió a donde estaban los doscientos hombres que habían estado demasiado agotados para seguirlo y se habían quedado en el arroyo de Besor. Ellos salieron a recibir a David y a las tropas que lo acompañaban, y David, al acercarse, los saludó.
es.R: David volvió a donde estaban los doscientos hombres que habían estado demasiado cansados para ir con él. Se habían quedado en el valle de Besor. Salieron a recibir a David y a los soldados que venían con él. David se acercó a ellos y los saludó con cariño.

fr.L: Et David arriva auprès des deux cents hommes qui avaient été trop épuisés pour suivre David, et qu’on avait fait rester au torrent de Bésor ; et ils sortirent à la rencontre de David et à la rencontre du peuple qui [était] avec lui. Et David s’approcha du peuple et leur demanda comment allait [leur] paix.
fr.B: Puis David revint auprès des deux cents hommes qui avaient été trop épuisés pour le suivre et qu’on avait laissés au torrent de Bésor. Ils sortirent à la rencontre de David et de la troupe qui l’accompagnait, et quand David s’approcha, il les salua.
fr.R: David est revenu auprès des deux cents hommes qui avaient été trop fatigués pour le suivre. Ils étaient restés au ravin de Bésor. Ils sont sortis à la rencontre de David et des soldats qui étaient avec lui. David s’est approché d’eux et les a salués chaleureusement.

sw.L: Daudi akafika kwa wale watu 200 waliokuwa wamechoka mno kumfuata Daudi, ambao waliwaacha kwenye kijito cha Besori; nao wakatoka kumlaki Daudi na kuwalaki watu waliokuwa pamoja naye. Daudi akawakaribia watu, akawauliza hali [yao].
sw.B: Kisha Daudi akarudi kwa wale watu 200 waliokuwa wamechoka mno kumfuata, walioachwa kwenye kijito cha Besori. Wakatoka kumlaki Daudi na askari waliokuwa pamoja naye, naye Daudi alipowakaribia akawasalimu.
sw.R: Daudi akarudi kwa wale watu 200 waliokuwa wamechoka sana kwenda pamoja naye. Walikuwa wamebaki kwenye bonde la Besori. Wakatoka kumlaki Daudi na askari waliokuwa pamoja naye. Daudi akawaendea, akawasalimu kwa upendo.

vi.L: Đa-vít đến với 200 người đã quá mệt mỏi không theo Đa-vít được, là những người họ đã để lại ở khe Bê-sô. Họ ra đón Đa-vít và đón dân chúng ở với ông. Đa-vít đến gần dân chúng và hỏi thăm họ có bình an không.
vi.B: Rồi Đa-vít trở lại với 200 người đã quá kiệt sức không theo ông được và đã ở lại tại khe Bê-sô. Họ ra đón Đa-vít và quân lính đi với ông. Khi Đa-vít đến gần, ông chào hỏi họ.
vi.R: Đa-vít trở lại với 200 người đã quá mệt không đi theo ông được. Họ đã ở lại thung lũng Bê-sô. Họ ra đón Đa-vít và quân lính đi với ông. Đa-vít đến gần và ân cần chào hỏi họ.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 너무 지쳐서 다윗을 따라가지 못하여 브솔 시내에 머물러 있게 했던 이백 명에게 왔다. 그러자 그들이 다윗과 그와 함께 있는 백성을 맞으러 나왔다. 그리고 다윗이 백성에게 다가가 그들에게 안부를 물었다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 다윗은 너무 지쳐서 자기를 따라오지 못하고 브솔 시내에 남아 있던 이백 명에게 돌아왔다. 그들은 다윗과 그와 함께 있던 군인들을 맞으러 나왔다. 다윗은 그들에게 다가가 안부를 물었다.
ko.R: 다윗은 너무 지쳐서 함께 가지 못했던 이백 명에게 돌아왔다. 그들은 브솔 골짜기에 남아 있었다. 그들은 다윗과 그와 함께 온 군인들을 맞으러 나왔다. 다윗은 그들에게 다가가서 반갑게 인사했다.

decisions.choice: asked them of peace: greeted them, asking how they were
decisions.reason: To "ask someone about peace" is the usual greeting, asking after their welfare (17:22; 25:5). David meets the men who stayed behind as friends, not as failures.

decisions.choice: they had made them stay: the 200 had been left behind by the others
decisions.reason: The verb means "caused to stay". The subject is not named; it is David's party, who left the exhausted men at the wadi (verses 9-10).

decisions.choice: the people: the 400 with David, then the 200 at the wadi
decisions.reason: The first "people" are David's 400 fighting men; the second time, "the people" David comes near to are the 200 who come out to meet him.

decisions.choice: troops (Balanced), soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

decisions.choice: greeted them warmly
decisions.reason: Readable adds "warmly" to give the sense of asking after their welfare (m1).

source.text: וַיַּ֜עַן כָּל־אִֽישׁ־רָ֣ע וּבְלִיַּ֗עַל מֵֽהָאֲנָשִׁים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלְכ֣וּ עִם־דָּוִד֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־הָלְכ֣וּ עִמִּ֔י לֹֽא־נִתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם מֵהַשָּׁלָ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִצַּ֑לְנוּ כִּֽי־אִם־אִ֤ישׁ אֶת־אִשְׁתּוֹ֙ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֔יו וְיִנְהֲג֖וּ וְיֵלֵֽכוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And answered every man evil and worthless of the men who had gone with David, and they said, Because that not they went with me, not we will give to them of the plunder which we have rescued, except each his wife and his children, and let them drive [them] off and go.

en.L: And every evil and worthless man among the men who had gone with David answered and said, "Because they did not go with me, we will not give them [any] of the plunder that we have recovered, except to each man his wife and his {{gender:children|sons}}; let them lead [them] away and go."
en.B: But every wicked and worthless man in the company that had gone with David said, "Since they did not go with us, we will not give them any of the plunder we recovered. Each man may take his wife and {{gender:children|sons}} and go."
en.R: But the evil troublemakers among the men who had gone with David said, "These men did not go with us. So we will not give them any of the things we got back. Each of them can take his wife and {{gender:children|sons}} and leave."

es.L: Y respondieron todos los hombres malos y perversos de entre los que habían ido con David, y dijeron: «Por cuanto no fueron conmigo, no les daremos del botín que hemos recuperado, sino a cada uno su mujer y sus hijos; que se los lleven y se vayan».
es.B: Pero todos los hombres malvados y perversos del grupo que había ido con David dijeron: «Como no vinieron con nosotros, no les daremos nada del botín que recuperamos. Que cada uno tome a su mujer y a sus hijos y se vaya».
es.R: Pero los malvados y alborotadores que había entre los hombres que habían ido con David dijeron: «Estos no fueron con nosotros. Así que no les daremos nada de lo que recuperamos. Que cada uno tome a su esposa y a sus hijos y se vaya».

fr.L: Et tous les hommes mauvais et vauriens parmi les hommes qui étaient allés avec David prirent la parole et dirent : « Puisqu’ils ne sont pas venus avec moi, nous ne leur donnerons rien du butin que nous avons repris, sauf à chacun sa femme et ses {{gender:enfants|fils}} ; qu’ils les emmènent et s’en aillent. »
fr.B: Mais tous les méchants et les vauriens parmi ceux qui étaient allés avec David dirent : « Puisqu’ils ne sont pas venus avec nous, nous ne leur donnerons rien du butin que nous avons repris. Que chacun prenne sa femme et ses {{gender:enfants|fils}} et s’en aille. »
fr.R: Mais les méchants et les vauriens parmi les hommes qui étaient allés avec David ont dit : « Ces hommes ne sont pas venus avec nous. Alors nous ne leur donnerons rien de ce que nous avons récupéré. Chacun peut prendre sa femme et ses {{gender:enfants|fils}} et partir. »

sw.L: Kila mtu mwovu na asiyefaa kitu miongoni mwa watu waliokwenda pamoja na Daudi akajibu, akasema, "Kwa sababu hawakwenda pamoja nami, hatutawapa [kitu] katika nyara tulizookoa, ila kila mtu mkewe na watoto wake; wawachukue, waende zao."
sw.B: Lakini kila mtu mwovu na asiyefaa kitu kati ya wale waliokwenda pamoja na Daudi akasema, "Kwa kuwa hawakwenda pamoja nasi, hatutawapa chochote katika nyara tulizozirudisha. Kila mtu na amchukue mkewe na watoto wake, aende zake."
sw.R: Lakini watu waovu na wakorofi kati ya wale waliokwenda pamoja na Daudi wakasema, "Watu hawa hawakwenda pamoja nasi. Kwa hiyo hatutawapa chochote katika vitu tulivyorudisha. Kila mmoja wao na amchukue mkewe na watoto wake, aondoke."

vi.L: Mọi kẻ gian ác và vô lại trong số những người đã đi với Đa-vít lên tiếng nói: "Vì họ không đi với tôi, chúng ta sẽ không cho họ chút chiến lợi phẩm nào chúng ta đã thu hồi, ngoại trừ vợ và con cái của mỗi người; hãy để họ dẫn đi mà đi."
vi.B: Nhưng mọi kẻ gian ác và vô lại trong số những người đã đi với Đa-vít nói: "Vì họ không đi với chúng ta, chúng ta sẽ không chia cho họ chút chiến lợi phẩm nào đã thu hồi được. Mỗi người chỉ được nhận lại vợ và con cái mình rồi đi."
vi.R: Nhưng những kẻ gian ác hay gây rối trong số những người đã đi với Đa-vít nói: "Những người này không đi với chúng ta. Vậy chúng ta sẽ không chia cho họ thứ gì chúng ta đã lấy lại. Mỗi người chỉ được dẫn vợ con mình rồi đi."

ko.L: 그러자 다윗과 함께 갔던 사람들 가운데 악하고 쓸모없는 사람들이 모두 대답하여 말했다. "그들이 나와 함께 가지 않았으니, 우리가 되찾은 전리품 가운데에서 아무것도 그들에게 주지 않겠다. 다만 각 사람에게 자기 아내와 자식들만 주어, 그들을 데리고 가게 하자."
ko.B: 그러나 다윗과 함께 갔던 사람들 가운데 악하고 쓸모없는 자들이 모두 말했다. "그들은 우리와 함께 가지 않았으니, 우리가 되찾은 전리품은 하나도 줄 수 없다. 저마다 자기 아내와 자식들만 데리고 떠나게 하자."
ko.R: 그러나 다윗과 함께 갔던 사람들 가운데 못된 불량배들이 말했다. "이 사람들은 우리와 함께 가지 않았다. 그러니 우리가 되찾은 물건은 하나도 줄 수 없다. 저마다 아내와 자식들만 데리고 떠나라고 하자."

decisions.choice: evil and worthless men: wicked men who reject what is right
decisions.reason: The word for "worthless" is the one used of Eli's sons (2:12), of those who despised Saul (10:27) and of Nabal (25:17, 25). "Every evil and worthless man" means all the men of that kind, not the whole 400.

decisions.choice: they did not go with me: the group speaks as one man
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "with me", as though each man spoke for himself or the group spoke with one voice. The ancient Greek translation reads "with us". The sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: his wife and his children; let them drive them off and go
decisions.reason: The word for "sons" here means children of both sexes, as in verse 19. "Drive off" is the verb of verse 2: the men may lead their families away but get nothing else.

decisions.choice: with us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural for a group speaking together (m2).

decisions.choice: ses {{gender:enfants|fils}}
decisions.reason: The word means children of both sexes (m3); as the English, the inclusive word is the default and "fils" the alternative.

decisions.choice: hombres malos y perversos; sus hijos, without a gender span
alternatives: a gender span on the children, as the English has
decisions.reason: Wicked men who reject what is right (m1), with the terms note's “perversos” for “sons of Belial”. The English has a gender span on “children”; Spanish “hijos” already covers sons and daughters, so no span is needed, as the Psalms note sets.

decisions.choice: "watoto" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The word here means children of both sexes (m3); Swahili "watoto" says it plainly, so there is no second wording for the gender setting to offer.

decisions.choice: "kẻ gian ác và vô lại"
decisions.reason: The terms note's word for worthless men. No gender span on "con cái": it already means sons and daughters, as at 17:53.

decisions.choice: "악하고 쓸모없는 사람들" (L, B), "불량배들" (R); "자식들" for "children / sons", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "불량배" is the word the terms of this translation set for "worthless men"; Korean "자식" already covers sons and daughters, so the English setting has no second Korean wording.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד לֹֽא־תַעֲשׂ֥וּ כֵ֖ן אֶחָ֑י אֵ֠ת אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לָ֨נוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁמֹ֣ר אֹתָ֔נוּ וַיִּתֵּ֗ן אֶֽת־הַגְּד֛וּד הַבָּ֥א עָלֵ֖ינוּ בְּיָדֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David, Not you shall do so, my brothers, with what has given Yahweh to us; and he has kept us and has given the band that came against us into our hand.

en.L: But David said, "You shall not do so, my brothers, with what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given us. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept us and has given the band that came against us into our hand.
en.B: But David said, "My brothers, you must not act this way with what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given us. He has kept us safe and has handed over to us the raiding party that came against us.
en.R: But David said, "My brothers, you must not do this. These things are what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given us. He kept us safe, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave us victory over the raiders who attacked us.

es.L: Pero dijo David: «No {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} así, hermanos míos, con lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos ha dado. Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos ha guardado y ha entregado en nuestra mano a la banda que vino contra nosotros.
es.B: Pero David dijo: «Hermanos míos, no {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} hacer esto con lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos ha dado. Él nos ha protegido y ha puesto en nuestras manos a la banda que vino contra nosotros.
es.R: Pero David dijo: «Hermanos míos, no {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} hacer esto. Todo esto nos lo ha dado {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Él nos protegió, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos dio la victoria sobre los saqueadores que nos atacaron.

fr.L: Mais David dit : « Vous ne ferez pas ainsi, mes frères, avec ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a donné. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a gardés et a livré dans notre main la bande qui était venue contre nous.
fr.B: Mais David dit : « Mes frères, vous ne devez pas agir ainsi avec ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a donné. C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui nous a protégés et qui nous a livré la bande qui nous avait attaqués.
fr.R: Mais David a dit : « Mes frères, vous ne devez pas faire cela. Ces choses, c’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui nous les a données. Il nous a protégés, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a donné la victoire sur les pillards qui nous avaient attaqués.

sw.L: Lakini Daudi akasema, "Msifanye hivyo, ndugu zangu, kwa vitu ambavyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametupa. Naye ametulinda, na amekitia mkononi mwetu kikosi kilichokuja juu yetu.
sw.B: Lakini Daudi akasema, "Ndugu zangu, msifanye hivyo kwa vitu ambavyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametupa. Yeye ametulinda salama, naye ametutia mikononi kikosi cha wavamizi kilichotushambulia.
sw.R: Lakini Daudi akasema, "Ndugu zangu, msifanye hivyo. Vitu hivi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ndiye aliyetupa. Alitulinda salama, naye akatupa ushindi juu ya wavamizi waliotushambulia.

vi.L: Nhưng Đa-vít nói: "Thưa anh em, anh em không được làm như vậy với những gì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ban cho chúng ta. {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã gìn giữ chúng ta và đã phó toán quân đến đánh chúng ta vào tay chúng ta.
vi.B: Nhưng Đa-vít nói: "Thưa anh em, anh em không được đối xử như vậy với những gì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ban cho chúng ta. {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã gìn giữ chúng ta an toàn và đã phó vào tay chúng ta toán quân cướp đã đến đánh chúng ta.
vi.R: Nhưng Đa-vít nói: "Thưa anh em, anh em không được làm như vậy. Những thứ này là do {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho chúng ta. {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã gìn giữ chúng ta an toàn, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã cho chúng ta thắng bọn cướp đã tấn công chúng ta.

ko.L: 그러자 다윗이 말했다. "내 형제들아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리에게 주신 것을 가지고 그렇게 하지 마라. 그분께서 우리를 지키시고, 우리를 치러 온 무리를 우리 손에 넘겨주셨다.
ko.B: 그러나 다윗이 말했다. "내 형제들아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리에게 주신 것을 가지고 그렇게 해서는 안 된다. 주님께서 우리를 지켜 주시고, 우리를 치러 온 약탈대를 우리 손에 넘겨주셨다.
ko.R: 그러나 다윗이 말했다. "내 형제들아, 그렇게 하면 안 된다. 이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리에게 주신 것이다. 주님께서 우리를 지켜 주셨고, 우리를 공격한 약탈자들을 이기게 해 주셨다.

decisions.choice: what the LORD has given us: the plunder is the LORD's gift, not the fighters' own winnings
decisions.reason: David answers that the plunder was not won by the strength of the 400. The LORD kept them alive and gave them the victory, so no one may claim it by right of his own effort.

decisions.choice: has given the band into our hand: has given us victory over them
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. To give an enemy into someone's hand is to let them defeat it (14:10; 23:4).

decisions.choice: my brothers: comrades
decisions.reason: David speaks to his men as fellow members of one company, not as their master. These are the men who wanted to stone him (verse 6).

decisions.choice: he, with a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The one who kept them and gave them victory is the LORD, so a pronoun for him inside a sentence takes the reader setting.

decisions.choice: gave us victory over
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m2).

decisions.choice: "anh em" for "my brothers"
decisions.reason: Comrades in arms (m3); David speaks to his men as one of them, as in 23:3.

decisions.choice: "내 형제들아" (my brothers), in the plain style
decisions.reason: David addresses his men as comrades (meaning decision m3); Korean keeps the family word, which carries the same warmth.

source.text: וּמִי֙ יִשְׁמַ֣ע לָכֶ֔ם לַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֞י כְּחֵ֣לֶק׀הַיֹּרֵ֣ד בַּמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וּֽכְחֵ֛לֶק הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב עַל־הַכֵּלִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֥ו יַחֲלֹֽקוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And who will listen to you in the matter the this? For as [the] share of the [one] going down into the battle, and as [the] share of the [one] staying by the baggage, together they shall share.

en.L: And who will listen to you in this matter? For as [is] the share of the one going down into the battle, so [is] the share of the one staying by the baggage; they shall share alike."
en.B: Who would listen to you in this matter? The share of the man who stays with the supplies is to be the same as the share of the man who goes down into battle. They will share alike."
en.R: No one will agree with you about this! The man who stays behind to guard the supplies will get the same share as the man who goes into battle. Everyone will share alike."

es.L: ¿Y quién {{plural_you:los|os}} escuchará en este asunto? Porque como [es] la parte del que baja a la batalla, así [es] la parte del que se queda con el equipaje; repartirán por igual».
es.B: ¿Quién {{plural_you:les|os}} va a hacer caso en esto? La parte del que se queda con las provisiones será igual a la parte del que baja a la batalla. Repartirán por igual».
es.R: ¡Nadie estará de acuerdo con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en esto! El que se queda atrás cuidando las provisiones recibirá la misma parte que el que va a la batalla. Todos recibirán lo mismo».

fr.L: Et qui vous écoutera dans cette affaire ? Car telle [est] la part de celui qui descend au combat, telle [est] la part de celui qui reste près des bagages ; ils partageront ensemble. »
fr.B: Qui donc vous écouterait sur ce point ? Celui qui reste près du matériel aura la même part que celui qui descend au combat. Ils partageront à égalité. »
fr.R: Personne ne sera d’accord avec vous ! L’homme qui reste en arrière pour garder le matériel aura la même part que celui qui va au combat. Tout le monde partagera de la même façon. »

sw.L: Na ni nani atakayewasikiliza katika jambo hili? Kwa maana kama lilivyo fungu la yule anayeshuka vitani, ndivyo litakavyokuwa fungu la yule anayekaa na mizigo; watagawana sawasawa."
sw.B: Ni nani angewasikiliza katika jambo hili? Fungu la mtu anayebaki na mizigo litakuwa sawa na fungu la mtu anayeshuka vitani. Watagawana sawasawa."
sw.R: Hakuna mtu atakayekubaliana nanyi katika jambo hili! Mtu anayebaki nyuma kulinda mizigo atapata fungu sawa na mtu anayekwenda vitani. Wote watagawana sawasawa."

vi.L: Ai sẽ nghe anh em trong việc này? Vì phần của người xuống trận thế nào, thì phần của người ở lại giữ hành lý cũng thế ấy; họ sẽ chia đều với nhau."
vi.B: Ai mà nghe anh em trong việc này? Phần của người ở lại giữ đồ tiếp tế phải bằng phần của người xuống trận. Họ sẽ chia đều với nhau."
vi.R: Không ai đồng ý với anh em về chuyện này đâu! Người ở lại canh giữ đồ tiếp tế sẽ nhận phần bằng người ra trận. Mọi người sẽ chia đều với nhau."

ko.L: 이 일에 누가 너희 말을 듣겠느냐? 싸움터에 내려간 사람의 몫과 같이, 물건 곁에 머문 사람의 몫도 [같으니], 그들이 똑같이 나누어야 한다."
ko.B: 이 일에 누가 너희 말을 듣겠느냐? 물건을 지키며 남아 있던 사람의 몫은 싸움터에 나간 사람의 몫과 같아야 한다. 모두 똑같이 나누어야 한다."
ko.R: 아무도 너희 말에 찬성하지 않을 것이다! 뒤에 남아서 물건을 지킨 사람도 싸움터에 나간 사람과 똑같은 몫을 받을 것이다. 모두 똑같이 나누어 가져야 한다."

decisions.choice: who will listen to you: a question that means no one will
decisions.reason: David's question expects the answer "no one": no one in Israel would accept the rule the worthless men propose.

decisions.choice: the one staying by the baggage: the man who guards the supplies
decisions.reason: The word means gear, equipment and supplies. Guarding them was a real duty in war (17:22; 25:13, where David leaves 200 men with the baggage).

decisions.choice: they shall share alike: one rule for those who fought and those who stayed
decisions.reason: The plunder from Midian was divided in a similar way between the fighters and the rest of the congregation (Numbers 31:27), and Joshua told the tribes going home to share their plunder with their brothers (Joshua 22:8). Verse 25 makes David's rule lasting law.

decisions.choice: the share of the man who stays ... the same as the share of the man who goes
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the man who stayed first, since he is the one whose share was in question; the meaning of the comparison is unchanged.

decisions.choice: No one will agree with you about this!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies (m1).

source.text: וַיְהִ֕י מֵֽהַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וָמָ֑עְלָה וַיְשִׂמֶ֜הָ לְחֹ֤ק וּלְמִשְׁפָּט֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it was from the day the that and onward, and he set it as a statute and as a judgment for Israel until the day the this.

en.L: And it was [so] from that day and onward; and he made it a statute and a judgment for Israel, to this day.
en.B: From that day on it was so: David made it a statute and a ruling for Israel, and it remains so to this day.
en.R: From that day on, David made this a law and a rule for Israel. It is still the rule to this day.

es.L: Y así fue desde aquel día en adelante; y lo puso por estatuto y norma para Israel hasta el día de hoy.
es.B: Desde aquel día fue así: David lo estableció como estatuto y norma para Israel, y así sigue siendo hasta el día de hoy.
es.R: Desde aquel día, David hizo de esto una ley y una norma para Israel. Todavía es la norma hasta el día de hoy.

fr.L: Et il en fut [ainsi] depuis ce jour-là et dans la suite ; et il en fit une prescription et une règle pour Israël, jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.B: Depuis ce jour, il en fut ainsi : David en fit une loi et une règle pour Israël, et il en est toujours ainsi aujourd’hui.
fr.R: À partir de ce jour-là, David en a fait une loi et une règle pour Israël. C’est encore la règle aujourd’hui.

sw.L: Ikawa [hivyo] tangu siku ile na kuendelea; akaifanya kuwa kanuni na hukumu kwa Israeli, mpaka siku hii ya leo.
sw.B: Tangu siku ile ikawa hivyo: Daudi akaifanya kuwa kanuni na agizo kwa Israeli, nayo inadumu mpaka leo.
sw.R: Tangu siku ile, Daudi akaifanya kuwa sheria na kanuni kwa Israeli. Bado ni kanuni mpaka leo.

vi.L: Từ ngày đó trở đi [là như vậy]; ông lập điều ấy làm luật lệ và phán quyết cho Y-sơ-ra-ên cho đến ngày nay.
vi.B: Từ ngày đó trở đi đều như vậy: Đa-vít lập điều ấy thành luật lệ và quy định cho Y-sơ-ra-ên, và vẫn còn như thế cho đến ngày nay.
vi.R: Từ ngày đó trở đi, Đa-vít lập điều này thành luật và quy tắc cho Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ngày nay quy tắc ấy vẫn còn.

ko.L: 그리고 그날부터 그 뒤로 그렇게 되었다. 그가 그것을 이스라엘의 규례와 법도로 정하여 오늘에 이르렀다.
ko.B: 그날부터 그렇게 되었다. 다윗은 그것을 이스라엘의 규례와 법도로 정했고, 그것이 오늘까지 이어지고 있다.
ko.R: 그날부터 다윗은 이것을 이스라엘의 법과 규칙으로 삼았다. 그것은 오늘날까지 규칙으로 지켜지고 있다.

decisions.choice: a statute and a judgment: a fixed rule and a binding decision
decisions.reason: The two words are often paired for the laws of Israel (Exodus 15:25; Joshua 24:25). The first means something fixed or set down; the second, a ruling that decides cases. Together they say that David's decision became the standing law for sharing plunder.

decisions.choice: he made it: David
decisions.reason: The subject is David. Before he is king he already acts as a ruler who sets law for Israel.

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the time the account was written
decisions.reason: As at 5:5, the phrase refers to the writer's own day, when the rule was still kept.

decisions.choice: David
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject (m2).

decisions.choice: a statute and a ruling (Balanced); a law and a rule (Readable)
decisions.reason: The pair follows the wording set for these two words: "statutes and judgments" at Literal, "statutes and rulings" at Balanced, "laws and rules" at Readable, here in the singular.

decisions.choice: une prescription et une règle (L); une loi et une règle (B, R)
decisions.reason: The pair of law words as the Pentateuch note sets ("la prescription, la loi; la règle"); "jusqu'à ce jour" is the writer's own day (m3).

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א דָוִד֙ אֶל־צִ֣קְלַ֔ג וַיְשַׁלַּ֧ח מֵֽהַשָּׁלָ֛ל לְזִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה לְרֵעֵ֣הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֤ה לָכֶם֙ בְּרָכָ֔ה מִשְּׁלַ֖ל אֹיְבֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And came David to Ziklag, and he sent of the plunder to [the] elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, Here, for you [is] a blessing from [the] plunder of [the] enemies of Yahweh,

en.L: And David came to Ziklag, and he sent some of the plunder to the elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, "Here [is] a blessing for you from the plunder of the enemies of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}",
en.B: Back in Ziklag, David sent part of the plunder to the elders of Judah, who were his friends, with the words, "Here is a gift for you, taken from the plunder of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s enemies."
en.R: When David got back to Ziklag, he sent some of the things they had taken to his friends, the elders of Judah. He told them, "Here is a gift for you. It comes from what we took from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s enemies."

es.L: Y llegó David a Siclag, y envió parte del botín a los ancianos de Judá, a sus amigos, diciendo: «He aquí una bendición para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} del botín de los enemigos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}»,
es.B: De vuelta en Siclag, David envió parte del botín a los ancianos de Judá, que eran sus amigos, con este mensaje: «Aquí {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} un regalo para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, tomado del botín de los enemigos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».
es.R: Cuando David regresó a Siclag, envió algunas de las cosas que habían recuperado a sus amigos, los ancianos de Judá. Les dijo: «Aquí {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} un regalo para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Viene de lo que les quitamos a los enemigos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».

fr.L: Et David arriva à Tsiqlag, et il envoya une partie du butin aux anciens de Juda, à ses amis, en disant : « Voici pour vous une bénédiction [prise] sur le butin des ennemis {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} »,
fr.B: De retour à Tsiqlag, David envoya une partie du butin aux anciens de Juda, qui étaient ses amis, avec ces mots : « Voici pour vous un présent pris sur le butin des ennemis {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: Quand David est revenu à Tsiqlag, il a envoyé une partie de ce qu’ils avaient pris à ses amis, les anciens de Juda. Il leur a dit : « Voici un cadeau pour vous. Il vient de ce que nous avons pris aux ennemis {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »

sw.L: Daudi akafika Siklagi, akapeleka sehemu ya nyara kwa wazee wa Yuda, rafiki zake, akisema, "Tazama, baraka kwa ajili yenu kutoka katika nyara za adui za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}},"
sw.B: Daudi aliporudi Siklagi, akapeleka sehemu ya nyara kwa wazee wa Yuda, waliokuwa rafiki zake, akisema, "Hii hapa zawadi kwa ajili yenu, kutoka katika nyara za adui za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: Daudi aliporudi Siklagi, akapeleka sehemu ya vitu walivyoteka kwa rafiki zake, wazee wa Yuda. Akawaambia, "Hii ni zawadi kwa ajili yenu. Imetoka katika vitu tulivyowateka adui za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

vi.L: Đa-vít đến Xiếc-lác, và gửi một phần chiến lợi phẩm cho các trưởng lão Giu-đa, là bạn bè ông, mà nói rằng: "Đây [là] món quà phước lành cho các ông, lấy từ chiến lợi phẩm của các kẻ thù của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}",
vi.B: Về đến Xiếc-lác, Đa-vít gửi một phần chiến lợi phẩm cho các trưởng lão Giu-đa, là bạn bè ông, kèm lời nhắn: "Đây là món quà gửi các ông, lấy từ chiến lợi phẩm của các kẻ thù của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."
vi.R: Khi về đến Xiếc-lác, Đa-vít gửi một số chiến lợi phẩm cho bạn bè ông là các trưởng lão Giu-đa. Ông nhắn: "Đây là món quà gửi các ông. Món quà này lấy từ những gì chúng tôi đã lấy được của các kẻ thù của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 시글락에 와서 전리품 가운데 일부를 유다의 장로들, 곧 자기 친구들에게 보내며 말했다. "보십시오, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 원수들에게서 빼앗은 전리품 가운데에서 여러분에게 드리는 선물입니다."
ko.B: 시글락으로 돌아온 다윗은 전리품 가운데 일부를 자기 친구들인 유다의 장로들에게 보내며 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 원수들에게서 빼앗은 전리품 가운데에서 여러분께 드리는 선물입니다."
ko.R: 다윗은 시글락으로 돌아오자 빼앗아 온 물건 가운데 일부를 자기 친구들인 유다의 장로들에게 보냈다. 다윗은 이렇게 전했다. "이것은 여러분께 드리는 선물입니다. 우리가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 원수들에게서 빼앗아 온 것입니다."

decisions.choice: a blessing: a gift given as a sign of goodwill
decisions.reason: A gift that carries good wishes is called a "blessing" (25:27, of Abigail's gift to David; Genesis 33:11).

decisions.choice: the enemies of the LORD: Amalek, the LORD's enemy since the exodus
decisions.reason: The LORD had sworn to war against Amalek (Exodus 17:14-16; 15:2-3). David presents the plunder as won in the LORD's war, a share in the LORD's victory.

decisions.choice: the elders of Judah, his friends: leaders of the towns of his own tribe
decisions.reason: The elders led the towns and clans. Most of the towns in verses 27-31 lie in the south of Judah, where David had moved about while he fled from Saul and where he had raided the enemies of Judah (27:8-10). Soon after, the men of Judah make him king at Hebron (2 Samuel 2:1-4).

decisions.choice: to his friends: the same people as the elders
decisions.reason: The phrase stands next to "the elders of Judah" and names them again. The ancient Greek translation reads "and to his friends", as if these were a second group.

decisions.choice: a gift
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "gift" for "blessing" in this sense (m1).

decisions.choice: una bendición (L); un regalo (B, R)
decisions.reason: A gift given as a sign of goodwill (m1); Literal keeps the Hebrew word “blessing”, and Balanced and Readable say “regalo”, as the English says “gift” (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: each verse of the list in verses 27-31 closes as its own sentence, with "[보냈다]" bracketed at Literal
alternatives: one sentence running from verse 26 to 31
decisions.reason: The Hebrew list hangs on the verb of verse 26; Korean ends a sentence with its verb, so each verse closes on its own, as the terms of this translation settle, as the English Readable does.

source.text: לַאֲשֶׁ֧ר בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֛ל וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרָמֽוֹת־נֶ֖גֶב וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּיַתִּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: to those who [were] in Bethel and to those who [were] in Ramoth of [the] Negev and to those who [were] in Jattir,

en.L: to those who [were] in Bethel, and to those who [were] in Ramoth of the Negev, and to those who [were] in Jattir,
en.B: He sent it to those in Bethel, in Ramoth of the Negev and in Jattir,
en.R: He sent gifts to the people in the towns of Bethel, Ramoth in the Negev and Jattir.

es.L: a los que [estaban] en Betel, y a los que [estaban] en Ramot del Néguev, y a los que [estaban] en Jatir,
es.B: Lo envió a los de Betel, a los de Ramot del Néguev y a los de Jatir,
es.R: Envió regalos a la gente de los pueblos de Betel, Ramot del Néguev y Jatir.

fr.L: à ceux qui [étaient] à Béthel, et à ceux qui [étaient] à Ramoth du Néguev, et à ceux qui [étaient] à Yattir,
fr.B: Il en envoya à ceux de Béthel, de Ramoth du Néguev et de Yattir,
fr.R: Il a envoyé des cadeaux aux habitants des villes de Béthel, de Ramoth dans le Néguev et de Yattir.

sw.L: kwa wale waliokuwa Betheli, na kwa wale waliokuwa Ramothi ya Negebu, na kwa wale waliokuwa Yatiri,
sw.B: Akapeleka kwa wale wa Betheli, wa Ramothi ya Negebu na wa Yatiri,
sw.R: Akawapelekea zawadi watu wa miji ya Betheli, Ramothi katika Negebu, na Yatiri.

vi.L: cho những người ở Bê-tên, cho những người ở Ra-mốt miền Nê-ghép, và cho những người ở Gia-tia,
vi.B: Ông gửi cho những người ở Bê-tên, ở Ra-mốt miền Nê-ghép và ở Gia-tia,
vi.R: Ông gửi quà cho dân trong các thành Bê-tên, Ra-mốt ở miền Nê-ghép, và Gia-tia.

ko.L: 벧엘에 있는 사람들과 네겝 라못에 있는 사람들과 얏딜에 있는 사람들에게 [보냈다].
ko.B: 그는 벧엘과 네겝 라못과 얏딜에 있는 사람들에게 보냈다.
ko.R: 그는 벧엘과 네겝의 라못과 얏딜 마을 사람들에게 선물을 보냈다.

decisions.choice: Bethel: a town in the south of Judah, not the Bethel north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The well-known Bethel lay in the north, far from the others in this list. A southern town called Bethul or Bethuel was in the land of Simeon (Joshua 19:4; 1 Chronicles 4:30), and the name here probably means that town. The ancient Greek translation reads Beth-zur, a town north of Hebron.

decisions.choice: Ramoth of the Negev; Jattir: towns in the south of Judah
decisions.reason: Ramoth of the Negev is probably the "Ramah of the Negev" in Simeon's land (Joshua 19:8). Jattir was a town in the hill country south of Hebron, later given to the priests (Joshua 15:48; 21:14).

decisions.choice: He sent it / He sent gifts
decisions.reason: The list continues the sentence begun in verse 26. Balanced and Readable start it again with "He sent", since the quotation stands between.

decisions.choice: one sentence for each verse of the list
decisions.reason: Readable gives each verse of the list its own short sentence (verses 27-31).

decisions.choice: Béthel, Ramoth du Néguev, Yattir; and in verses 28-30 Aroër, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa, Rakal, Horma, Bor-Ashân, Atak
decisions.reason: Béthel as the Samuel terms note sets; the other towns, not in the table, in the usual French transcription.

decisions.choice: "Betheli", "Ramothi ya Negebu", "Yatiri" (and the towns of verses 28-30)
decisions.reason: "Betheli" as the terms note; the other towns take a Swahili spelling with a final vowel where Swahili writes one.

decisions.choice: "Bê-tên", "Ra-mốt miền Nê-ghép", "Gia-tia" and the towns of verses 28-31
decisions.reason: "Bê-tên" as the Vietnamese Genesis (here a town in the south, m1); the other towns of this list take the usual Protestant forms: A-rô-e, Síp-mốt, Ếch-tê-mô-a, Ra-canh, Họt-ma, Bô-a-san, A-tác, Hếp-rôn.

decisions.choice: Racal: a town named only here
decisions.reason: Racal is not named elsewhere. The ancient Greek translation reads Carmel, the town of Nabal and Abigail south of Hebron (25:2).

decisions.choice: the Jerahmeelites and the Kenites: clans living in the south of Judah
decisions.reason: The Jerahmeelites were a clan of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:9, 25-27), and the Kenites were the clan linked to Moses by marriage (15:6; Judges 1:16). David had told Achish that he raided these very peoples (27:10); in fact he now sends them gifts.

decisions.choice: Hebron: the chief town of Judah
decisions.reason: Hebron, the old town where Abraham lived and Caleb settled (Genesis 23:2; Joshua 14:13), comes last in the list. David is soon made king there (2 Samuel 2:1-4).

decisions.choice: had gone about: had moved from place to place
decisions.reason: The verb means to walk about or go to and fro. It sums up David's years as a fugitive, when he and his men went wherever they could (23:13).

decisions.choice: had stayed
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for the places where David and his men spent time as they moved about.
